data.text:
Spike results (throwaway probe test, deleted; re-derivable from this note). Ran with
`swift test --filter ScratchProbeTests` (sandbox off) on macOS 26.5 / Xcode 26.

KNOWN RISK RESOLVED — NO PUMP NEEDED. A plain `@MainActor` async swift-testing
test receives every WebKit delegate callback: didFinish fired 0.16 s after
loadHTMLString, http loads settle, dialogs fire, callAsyncJavaScript resolves,
Task.sleep works. Swift Testing's main-actor executor drains the main queue and
WebKit's IPC is serviced. The wire spike's `RunLoop.main.run()` requirement
applies to *executables* (dispatchMain), not to the test harness. No helper added
to Tests/TestSupport; verb families can write ordinary @MainActor async tests.

Probe facts, each demonstrated:
- httpStatus: WKNavigationDelegate decidePolicyFor navigationResponse, isForMainFrame,
  response as HTTPURLResponse. 200 and 404 both delivered; a 404 still *finishes*
  the navigation (WebKit renders the error body) — 404 is not a loadFailure.
- unroutable port (127.0.0.1:65533) -> didFailProvisionalNavigation,
  NSURLErrorDomain -1004 "Could not connect to the server."
  CAUTION: 127.0.0.1:**1** is on WebKit's blocked-port list and behaves oddly —
  tests must use a closed high port.
- dialogs.html?auto: all three WKUIDelegate panels fire during load; declining
  gives the page `confirm:false; prompt:null`. Load still finishes.
- NSAppearance(named: .aqua/.darkAqua) set on the WKWebView works headless with no
  NSApplication: theme.html resolved "light" vs "dark".
- Hanging load (/delay/600000/): NO delegate callback ever arrives. stopLoading()
  produces didFail -999 (cancelled). So the host must own the clock, stop the load,
  and ignore the trailing cancellation.
- `URL.appendingPathComponent("dialogs.html?auto")` percent-encodes the `?`;
  use URL(string:relativeTo:) for query fixtures.
- WKUIDelegate completion handlers are typed `@escaping @MainActor @Sendable`;
  the delegate must match exactly or Swift silently declines the conformance
  (warning only, then no dialogs).

DESIGN DECISION — console capture must live in the PAGE world, not an isolated one.
The brief specified "a document-start hook in an isolated world". Demonstrated wrong:
an isolated world has its own `console` global, so overriding `console.error` there
never sees the page's calls. Probe result — with the same page calling console.error
and throwing an uncaught error, the isolated-world override received nothing while a
page-world override received the call. (The `window` 'error' *event* IS visible from
an isolated world, since content worlds share the DOM; only JS globals are separate.)
Same root cause as the wire spike's fetch-recorder finding.

Consequence: PageHost installs ONE namespaced page-world document-start script
(`window.__sleepyHollow`) that wraps console.error and listens for 'error' and
'unhandledrejection'. Keeping all three in one world avoids double counting.

DESIGN DECISION — the count is pulled, not pushed. WKScriptMessage delivery is not
ordered against didFinish, so counting host-side from messages would be racy. The
page-world script keeps its own counter and PageHost reads it with one
callAsyncJavaScript round-trip after settle — deterministic. The script *also* posts
every error to the message handler `sleepyhollow.console`, so the console verb leaf
(zffuW) gets a live stream for free without changing the Host.

Integration review finding to harden when this family wires action steps: SleepyCLIKit's ActionStepParser scans the raw argument vector, so a VALUE of an unrelated flag that lexically equals --click/--fill/--submit (e.g. --prompt-text '--click') is misparsed as a step and swallows the next token; the parser also ignores the `--` terminator. Fix by teaching the scanner which preceding tokens are value-taking options (or by consuming ArgumentParser's parsed arrays for counts and argv only for order), and honor `--`. Regression tests first per TDD.

SEAM SIGNATURES (settled — leaves oCDLF/ta55o/UcahB/Jvkzu/q6mlw/zffuW/XDmfo/5Kfpm build on these).
All on `@MainActor public final class PageHost`:

  public init(options: LoadOptions = LoadOptions())
  public let options: LoadOptions
  public let webView: WKWebView              // see note below
  public private(set) var facts: PageFacts
  public var budget: TimeInterval            // options.budget ?? LoadOptions.defaultBudget
  public static let consoleMessageName = "sleepyHollowConsole"

  @discardableResult public func load(_ url: URL) async throws -> PageFacts
  public func install(_ script: InjectedScript)                     // must precede the load
  @discardableResult public func evaluate(
      _ body: String,
      arguments: [String: Any] = [:],
      in world: InjectedScript.World = .isolated) async throws -> String   // JSON text
  public func messages(named: String, in world: InjectedScript.World = .isolated) -> AsyncStream<String>
  public func execute<O: ExecutablePageOperation>(_ operation: O) async throws -> O.Output

  public protocol ExecutablePageOperation: PageOperation {
      @MainActor func execute(on host: PageHost) async throws -> Output
  }
  @MainActor public extension InjectedScript.World { var contentWorld: WKContentWorld }
  @MainActor public extension ColorTheme { var appearanceName: NSAppearance.Name }

DECISION — `webView` is public, beyond the brief's list. The capture, find and cookie
families need WKWebView's own APIs (takeSnapshot, createPDF, createWebArchive, find,
WKHTTPCookieStore); a wrapper that only forwarded them would be an adapter holding no
decision. Navigation stays in load(_:) — loading through the property bypasses the
budget and the facts, and the DocC says so.

DECISION — `evaluate` stringifies page-side and returns JSON text. Implementation wraps
the caller's body in `await (async () => { … })()`; the arrow captures lexically so the
named `arguments` WebKit puts in scope stay visible and `await` still works. `undefined`
and unstringifiable values come back as "null". Page exceptions propagate as WebKit's own
WKError — deliberately unwrapped, so the eval verb (q6mlw) shapes them rather than the
host guessing.

DECISION — the timeout's "last state" is on the host, not in the error. SleepyError is a
frozen Core type with no facts field, and the host outlives the throw, so `host.facts`
after a catch IS the attachment. Caveat documented in DocC: consoleErrorCount is 0 on a
timeout, because reading it needs a round-trip to a page that just proved it will not
answer.

DECISION — `load` refuses re-entry with a usage error. Found by testing, not by reading:
two overlapping loads dropped the first CheckedContinuation and the test *hung forever*.
The guard is a plain Bool set synchronously before the first suspension.

CRITERIA FACTUALLY MET (integrator to mark; full suite green: 61 tests, 16 suites,
`swift test` with the sandbox disabled; `swiftformat . --lint --config .swiftformat`
clean; `swift package generate-documentation --target SleepyHollow` warning-free).

A4R loads a fixture headless and reports final URL, status, console-error count —

xgo a hanging load becomes a structured timeout, never a hang —
  PageHostLoadTests "a hanging load becomes a timeout well inside the fixture's delay"

  is a load failure with a next move" (.loadFailure) and "a second load while one is in

E10 dialog fixture shows decline-and-record defaults and flag overrides —
  PageHostDialogTests: dialogs.html?auto records alert/confirm/prompt as
  acknowledged/dismissed/dismissed and the page sees `confirm:false; prompt:null`; with
  acceptsConfirms + promptResponse it records accepted/answered and the page sees

kOO theme fixture renders differently under light and dark —
  PageHostThemeTests: theme.html resolves "light" vs "dark", and light is the default.

BEFOREUNLOAD FINDING (the brief asked me to investigate). WKUIDelegate has NO public
beforeunload hook. The only public `runBeforeUnloadConfirmPanelWithMessage:` in the macOS
26.5 SDK is on the legacy `WebUIDelegate`/`WebView` pair (WebUIDelegate.h:402);
WKWebView's equivalent is SPI (`_webView:runBeforeUnloadConfirmPanel…`). Unimplemented,
WebKit leaves the page — which is exactly the vision's stated policy, so the *outcome* is
right even though nothing is observable. Consequence for the output shape:
DialogRecord.Kind.beforeUnload can never be produced from public API, and a beforeunload
handler cannot stall a navigation. Demonstrated by a new fixture (before-unload.html) and
a test that navigates away from it. If the vision wants beforeunload *recorded*, that
needs SPI and a conscious decision; recommend documenting the case as unreachable
instead.

Transport spike (scratchpad prototypes, macOS 26.5, Network.framework):
- NWListener with NWParameters.requiredLocalEndpoint = .unix(path:) DOES work for a
  Unix socket, and a plain NWConnection(to: .unix(path:)) connects. Chosen transport.
- Trap 1: NWListener never unlinks the socket file on cancel, and re-binding over ANY
  existing file at the path fails EADDRINUSE (48) regardless of allowLocalEndpointReuse.
  => SessionHost must probe for a live owner, then unlink the stale path before binding.
- Trap 2: a connection to a dead/absent unix socket goes to .waiting(ECONNREFUSED),
  NOT .failed — NW retries forever. => the client must treat .waiting as a failure or
  it hangs (the one thing the vision forbids).
- Trap 3: NWConnection(to: .unix(path:)) with a path longer than sun_path (104 bytes)
  CRASHES the process (SIGTRAP inside Network); the listener merely lies about being
  ready. => registry validates socket path length up front with a teaching error, and
  the socket file is named "sock" to keep the path short.

Design decisions before code (observe family):

1. PULL, not push, is the authority. Script messages are not ordered against didFinish and no sink exists during a one-shot load, so both verbs read page-world state after settle (the doctrine ConsoleCapture already documents for its error count). The wire recorder still POSTS the spike's three messages (request/response/body) for live/session consumers - a test subscribes and asserts that shape - but assembles them by id into its own buffer, which is what the host reads. Deviation from the spike's "the host assembles the three messages by id": assembly happens in the recorder's own state; the host applies the honest-reporting pass (missing body after a response => truncated: "budget").

2. Recorder installation. The recorder must be a document-start user script, so it cannot be installed by an operation that runs after the load. PageHost.swift is frozen (wait agent), so it is installed through LoadOptions: new LoadOptions.recordingWire(byteCap:) in Operations/LoadOptions+Wire.swift, called by WireCommand. WireOperation throws a teaching .environment error when the recorder is absent. NEED FOR PageHost (noted, not built): once PageHost is unfrozen, installing the recorder there (as ConsoleCapture is) would make `wire --session` work without the session leaf remembering to opt in.

3. Host-side settle inside WireOperation. The wait engine is not landed, and fetch.html fires its requests on the load event - i.e. after didFinish - so a naive read returns an empty log. WireOperation polls the recorder over a host-owned budget (default 2000 ms) until it is quiet (no in-flight fetch, no pending body read, and >= 50 ms since the last activity), per the spike's "host-side deadlines only". No page-side timers are used.

4. ConsoleCapture.swift extended ADDITIVELY (the one Host/ file the brief allows): it now wraps console.log/info/warn/error/debug and buffers entries (level, origin, text, time, capped) alongside the existing errorCount, which still counts only errors + uncaught + unhandledrejection. Posted message kinds widen from console.error to console.<level>, which makes one sentence of PageHost.consoleMessageName's DocC incomplete - flagged for the integrator, since PageHost.swift is frozen.

Wait engine landed: .selector, .predicate, .idle inside PageHost's load pipeline; the wait guard in validateSupportedOptions() is gone. New: Host/WaitEngine.swift, Host/SelectorWatch.swift, Host/IdleWatch.swift; PageHost gains a private `waiter` and two lines in load(). One deadline (DispatchTime.now() + budget) covers navigation and settle together. MECHANISMS, measured not assumed (probes deleted; findings in project/2026-08-20-wait-engine.md): - selector = isolated-world MutationObserver posting a script message, PLUS a 250ms host-side re-check. Both are load-bearing and each is proven by a test that fails without it: neutering the backstop leaves #late settling on the push at ~300ms but #agree:checked timing out, because assigning the IDL property `checked` produces no mutation record at all. - predicate = host-side evaluate every 50ms, IN THE PAGE WORLD (decision worth review: the vision defaults `sleepy eval` to the isolated world, but a wait predicate is a statement about the page's own state and an isolated world reads every page global as undefined - a silently wrong answer). A throwing predicate counts as "not true yet"; the last JS failure is quoted in the timeout message. An invalid SELECTOR, by contrast, is a usage error on the first check. - idle contract (also in DocC and the findings doc): idle = 500ms on the HOST clock with no new PerformanceResourceTiming entry, no fetch or XHR starting or finishing, and nothing outstanding (zero fetch/XHR in flight, every complete). Window starts at the settle phase, so --wait-for idle always costs >= 500ms. Blind to workers/service workers, WebSocket/EventSource; a fetch is "finished" when its promise settles, not when the body is read. A page that requests something once a second IS idle by this contract. CORRECTION TO THE WIRE SPIKE (edited in place as a marked block quote): page timers are NOT throttled in this host. With zero host evaluation after didFinish, setTimeout(400) fired at 400ms and setTimeout(1500) at 1501ms; pumping at 250ms/50ms changed nothing; network completions also arrive unpumped. What never fires headless is requestAnimationFrame. Briefs telling agents to avoid setTimeout in fixtures are backwards. Criteria, factually: LK2 met (all four kinds against fixtures: 15 new host tests + 4 CLI golden tests). 6dF met at the library layer (timeout kind = .timeout -> ExitStatus 3, facts.finalURL and facts.httpStatus recorded BEFORE settling so the last state survives the throw; the page is deliberately not stopped so it stays readable) and end to end (golden test asserts exit 3 with the selector named in stderr). OSD met: nothing outside PageHost changed; `sleepy load --wait-for` works with LoadFlagOptions untouched. TEST DEBT REMOVED: PageHostScopeTests' "wait conditions beyond load are refused, naming the wait-engine leaf" is deleted - it asserted the guard this leaf removes. FLAKINESS WARNING for future leaves: wall-clock assertions inflate 2-3x in the full parallel suite (one main actor, ~130 WebKit tests). Recorded in gotchas.md.

Full suite: 145 tests green (was 112); swiftformat --lint clean; DocC generates without warnings.

Protocol: 4-byte big-endian length + JSON. SessionRequest = .operation(OperationEnvelope) |
.shutdown; SessionReply = .output(Data) | .acknowledged | .failure(SleepyError). One
connection per request (a CLI invocation is the natural connection lifetime).

Layout: <root>/sessions/<name>/{sock, session.json}. session.json is a Friendly
SessionRecord {processID, url, startedAt, idleTimeout} — it replaces a bare pid file and
gives `sessions list` its columns. Root override: SLEEPYHOLLOW_HOME or
SessionRegistry(root:). Liveness = kill(pid,0) AND connect() to the socket; classified as
live / noRecord / deadProcess / unreachableSocket. prune() removes anything not live plus
directories with no readable record.

TTL: SessionHost.defaultIdleTimeout = 15*60, one constant; --idle-timeout overrides and a
non-positive value is refused (an unreapable helper is exactly the orphan we forbid).
Idle clock resets on every request; SessionHost.bindTimeout = 10s bounds startup.

For the verbs leaf (DLHu7):
- SessionOperations.registry is the assembly point — register your ExecutablePageOperation
  there and --session works with no other wiring.
- `sleepy _host --name <n> [--url <u>] [--idle-timeout <s>] [--home <path>] <load flags>`
  writes one line of JSON (the SessionRecord) to stdout, unbuffered, when it is READY
  (socket bound AND first load finished), then serves. `open` can read that line instead
  of polling. A failed first load: helper cleans up and exits with the load's exit code.
- Requests that arrive during startup are answered after the first load completes, never
  against a blank page.
- SessionClient(name:registry:).run(op) / .shutdown(); errors are teaching SleepyErrors.
- Not built (deliberately, out of scope): SIGTERM handling in the helper — `close` should
  use the shutdown frame, not a signal, or the directory is left for prune.

Criteria factually met (integrator marks them):
- 6Bh: `a spawned helper serves an operation over its socket` (SessionProtocolGoldenTests)
  spawns the real `sleepy _host`, ships ReadFactsOperation over the socket, gets PageFacts
  back with httpStatus 200 from a fixture page; plus the in-process equivalent in

- eNu: `a short-TTL helper self-terminates and cleans up` (2s TTL, real binary, exit 0,
  directory gone) and `an idle host self-terminates and cleans up after its TTL` (1s,
  in-process), plus `work restarts the idle clock` proving idleness is what expires.
- M3S: `a kill -9'd helper is detected as dead and pruned` (real binary, SIGKILL, registry
  reports .deadProcess and prune() removes it), plus registry-level unit tests for a stale
  record and a socketless one.
Known limits, all documented in code: two helpers racing to claim one name have a
microsecond-wide window between unlink and bind; the client has no reply deadline (the
host owns the clock, per the brief); SIGKILL/SIGTERM leave a directory for prune.

I6o element capture crops to the element rect on a fixture placed below the fold — Tests/TestSupport/Fixtures/capture-tall.html has #target at top:2400px in a 3000px document (well below the default 800pt viewport). ShotOperation(element:) measures getBoundingClientRect() and crops via WKSnapshotConfiguration.rect; verified both by unit test (CaptureShotOperationTests) and golden test (CaptureGoldenTests) that the output PNG is ~200x150px matching the fixture box, and differs from the viewport shot.

5o0 full-page capture exceeds viewport height on a long fixture — ShotOperation(fullPage: true) resizes host.webView.frame to document.documentElement.scrollHeight before snapshotting, restores after. Verified: capture is >=2900px tall on the 3000px fixture, and the host's viewport is restored afterward.

HlK pdf and archive emit valid artifacts via --out — PDFOperation wraps WKWebView.pdf(configuration:); ArchiveOperation wraps createWebArchiveData via a checked continuation (no async overload exists in the SDK). Golden tests write both via --out and verify: PDF starts with %PDF- and is >512 bytes; archive parses as a plist with a WebMainResource dict whose WebResourceURL matches the loaded page.

Key decisions (full detail in report to the dispatcher):
- --element not-found is ShotOperation.ElementNotFoundError (NOT a SleepyError — none of Core's 4 kinds fit "well-formed selector, page loaded, nothing matched"). ShotCommand catches it and calls Darwin.exit(1) directly, bypassing SleepyCommand.main()'s generic catch, which maps any non-SleepyError to exit 2 ("didn't understand that invocation") — wrong for a clean negative. This is a real seam gap: SleepyError.Kind has no case mapping to ExitStatus.negative (1); every future clean-negative verb (query --exists, find) will hit the same problem and needs the same workaround, or Core needs a Kind for it.
- takeSnapshot rasterizes at the *host Mac's* screen backing scale factor (measured 2560x1600 for a 1280x800pt viewport on a Retina host), not 1pt=1px, even though the view is never attached to a screen. WKSnapshotConfiguration.snapshotWidth does NOT fix this (only relabels NSImage's logical size). Fixed by re-rendering into a fresh NSBitmapImageRep at the exact target pixel size before PNG encoding. Recorded in project/gotchas.md — this could bite any other family that screenshots.
- Golden tests that shell out to the sleepy binary contend for real WebKit resources under swift test's default parallel execution: ~11+ concurrent `sleepy` subprocess launches, each with its own WKWebView, occasionally blow the 30s default budget under load. Design (jars agent, pre-implementation). Decisions where the vision doc is silent:

MECHANISM. macOS 12 floor rules out WKWebsiteDataStore(forIdentifier:) (14+), so the
data store stays nonPersistent() and the jar is a file SleepyHollow imports/exports
itself through WKHTTPCookieStore. That is also what keeps "bare invocation writes
nothing" true by construction: the jar code is only reached when options.jar != nil.

FORMAT. <home>/jars/<name>/cookies.json holding a CookieJarFile {version, updatedAt,
cookies: [CookieRecord]}, atomic write, sorted keys. CookieRecord is a Friendly struct
(name, value, domain, path, expiresAt, isSecure, isHTTPOnly, sameSite) that converts
to/from HTTPCookie. Directory-per-jar mirrors sessions/<name>/ and leaves room for
localStorage later.

TIMING. Import once per host, before the first navigation. Export at the end of
load() -- after settle and after runActionSteps -- so Set-Cookie during load and
document.cookie writes during settle/steps are both captured. load() also exports on
its throwing paths (timeout, load failure) but swallows write errors there: a login
that redirected and then timed out has still minted the cookie. PageHost.saveJar() is
public so a verb that mutates cookies after load (cookies set <url> --jar) can flush.

HYGIENE. Expired cookies are pruned on both read and write. Session cookies (no
expiry) ARE persisted -- a jar exists so a minted login survives, and most auth
cookies are session cookies; dropping them would defeat the flagship criterion.

GRAMMAR. sleepy jars list|clear <name>|rm <name>; name is a positional because
management verbs have no page source to contend for the bare slot (the flag-grammar
ruling is about page verbs). clear empties the cookies and keeps the jar; rm deletes
the directory. Unknown jar for clear/rm/cookies-get = environment, exit 5.
sleepy cookies get [<url>] [--jar n] [--name c]; sleepy cookies set [<url>] [--jar n]
--name --value [--domain --path --secure --http-only --max-age <seconds>].
With no page source, --jar is required and the command is pure file work; with a URL
it runs a CookiesOperation against the live store and flushes to the jar if named.
--max-age (seconds) rather than an ISO date: it is Set-Cookie's own vocabulary.
"Naming creates" applies to attaching (--jar on a loading verb always writes the jar,
even empty); reading an unknown jar is a typo, so it errors rather than returning [].

NEW FILES OUTSIDE THE LISTED SET (flagged): Host/PageHost+Cookies.swift (new file,
the WKHTTPCookieStore bridge + import/export, keeping PageHost.swift under the size
ceiling; no existing Host/ file edited except PageHost.swift). GoldenBinary gains an
additive optional `environment:` parameter so golden tests can set SLEEPYHOLLOW_HOME.

Golden e2e determinism suite built as two new files:
  Tests/SleepyGoldenTests/ByteStabilityGoldenTests.swift      (8 tests: load, dom, query, style, theme, find, ax, eval)
  Tests/SleepyGoldenTests/ArtifactDeterminismGoldenTests.swift (9 tests: console, wire, shot, pdf, archive, jars list, cookies get)
Every verb x format runs the SAME argv twice in two fresh subprocesses at
--size 1280x800 --theme light --budget 60000 and asserts byte-identity plus a
shape assertion. Full suite: 466 tests / 77 suites green (was 449/75), 31.4s
(was ~25s); the two new suites alone are 10.2s in isolation.

THREE DETERMINISM VIOLATIONS FOUND. None is fixable in output *rendering*
alone - each would change what data is reported - so per the brief they are
pinned as shape, not softened, and are the integrator's to rule on:

1. `console --format json` embeds `timeMilliseconds` (performance.now()).
   Observed 7 and 8 across eight runs of console-errors.html. The terse
   format never prints it and IS byte-stable. Ruling needed: keep the field
   (accept that json is not byte-stable), quantize it, or move it behind a
   flag.

2. `wire` (both formats) embeds startTime, duration, elapsedMilliseconds,
   startedAtMilliseconds and the whole `timing` block. Worse than numbers
   moving: the timing block's MEMBERSHIP moves, because a phase WebKit
   reports as 0 is dropped as absent, so a reused connection loses
   connectStart/connectEnd entirely and the JSON gains/loses five keys
   between runs. The terse line prints `Nms`. Ruling needed - though wire's
   whole point is the variance, so "excluded from the default output" is
   probably wrong here and "documented as exempt from rule 1" may be right.

3. `pdf` - WKWebView.createPDF stamps /CreationDate, /ModDate and a
   content-plus-date /ID into the trailer. Two runs of `pdf static.html`
   differed in exactly 66 bytes of 24286, all inside those three values;
   byte LENGTH, page count, page text and media box were identical. Ruling
   needed: rewrite the trailer metadata to a fixed value (PDFKit can), or
   document PDF as exempt.

NOT violations (measured, all byte-stable across repeated fresh
subprocesses): load, dom (html+json), query (json+text), style (json+text),
find (text+json), ax (outline+json), eval (json+text), console --format text,
shot PNG (byte-identical, 1280x800), archive .webarchive (byte-identical),
jars list (text+json), cookies get (text+json). Ordering was checked
separately and is stable everywhere: wire inventory order, wire fetches
order, console message order, multi-element query order. JarStore.names(),
JarStore.summaries() and CookiesOperation already sort. So NO output-
normalization fix was needed and none was made - Sources/ is untouched.

Caveat worth knowing: violations 1 and 2 are INTERMITTENT. On an idle machine
consecutive runs often quantize to the same millisecond - six mutated runs
with the normalization removed all passed. A plain byte-equality assertion on
console --format json or wire would therefore be a latent flake that reads as
contention rather than as a broken contract. That is why they are normalized
rather than pinned, and each normalized comparison carries a self-check that
the normalization actually bit.

Design (main thread, 2026-08-28):

- Opt-in, lazy, per operation — not a LoadOptions field and not the default. `PageHost.ensureOffscreenWindow()` (in a new `PageHost+Window.swift`) attaches the existing web view to an `OffscreenWindow` on first call and is idempotent; PDFOperation and later --scale / the time-series spike call it. Reason: hosting every page in a window would change every verb's timer/rAF behaviour at once; the spike measures that first, and flipping the default is a separate, documented decision.
- `OffscreenWindow` is a new @MainActor final class in Sources/SleepyHollow/Host/OffscreenWindow.swift: borderless NSWindow at (-20000,-20000), isReleasedWhenClosed=false, activation policy .prohibited set on NSApplication.shared before the window exists, never makeKey/activate. Whether it must be ordered (orderFrontRegardless) for WebKit to treat the view as visible is a measurement the leaf must make and record.
- "Nothing visible" is proven as: window.screen == nil (intersects no screen), NSApp.isActive == false throughout, activationPolicy == .prohibited, and no window whose frame intersects any NSScreen. That is the test.
- Finding doc: project/2026-08-28-offscreen-window-host.md — rAF, CSS transitions, backingScaleFactor / raw snapshot pixel size, and the ordering requirement, each with the command that reproduces it. Correct gotchas.md's rAF entry in place if rAF advances in the hosted view.

data.text:
Fixed on wt/helper (worktree .claude/worktrees/helper); not committed.

Cause confirmed exactly as filed: `SessionLauncher.currentExecutable()` built a URL
from `CommandLine.arguments[0]`. Under a `$PATH` lookup argv[0] is the bare word
`sleepy`, so `URL(fileURLWithPath:)` resolved it against cwd and `open` died with
"Couldn't start a session helper from '<cwd>/sleepy'" (exit 5).

Fix (Sources/SleepyHollow/Session/SessionLauncher.swift): resolve the running image
instead of the argument vector.

  currentExecutable() -> resolveExecutable(bundleExecutable: Bundle.main.executableURL,
                                           argument0: CommandLine.arguments.first)
  resolveExecutable(bundleExecutable:argument0:)  // internal, pure, symlink-resolving

Chose `Bundle.main.executableURL` over `_NSGetExecutablePath` / `proc_pidpath`:
a probe binary run as a bare PATH name from `/` showed all three return the same
absolute path (and the same path through a PATH symlink), so the tie-break is
idiomatics — Bundle is Foundation, needs no C buffer dance, and reads the same
dyld record `_NSGetExecutablePath` does. argv[0] survives only as the fallback
for "no main bundle". Symlinks are resolved because `$PATH` entries usually are
links (~/.swiftpm/bin, Homebrew shims). Rationale is in the DocC comment.

Tests (red first, both observed failing before the fix):
- Tests/SleepyGoldenTests/SessionLauncherPathGoldenTests.swift — regression. Spawns
  the built binary through `/usr/bin/env sleepy ...` (env does the PATH lookup and
  execs with argv[0] = "sleepy", exactly as a shell does) with cwd set to the temp
  dir, PATH prepended with the products dir. Red run reproduced the reported string
  verbatim; green now. Inside FixtureServer.withRunning, --budget 60000, closes the
  session, no Process.waitUntilExit after an await on the cooperative pool.
- Tests/SleepyHollowTests/SessionLauncherTests.swift — 5 unit tests over the pure
  rule (bare argv0, relative argv0, nil-bundle fallback, absoluteness, real file).

Also verified by hand outside the suite: symlink .build/debug/sleepy into a PATH dir,
`cd /`, `sleepy open https://example.com --name pc` -> exit 0 with page facts. No
stray helpers left.

Done on wt/sandbox (not committed). A sandbox launch denial now exits 4 with "WebKit could not start under this sandbox", not exit 3.

## The signal, measured 2026-08-28 in this worktree

Repro: `.build/debug/sleepy load file://…/Tests/TestSupport/Fixtures/static.html --budget 5000`, run inside Claude Code's Bash sandbox, with temporary probe logging in every WKNavigationDelegate callback.

Sandboxed (before the fix), stderr verbatim:

    Could not create a 'com.apple.coreservices.launchservicesd' sandbox extension
    Could not create a 'com.apple.coreservices.launchservicesd' sandbox extension
    PROBE webContentProcessDidTerminate
    file:///…/static.html did not finish loading within 5.0s. Raise the budget, or state the condition you are waiting for with --wait-for.
    EXIT=3

That launchservicesd line is printed twice, by WebKit, before any callback. The only delegate callback that ever fires is `webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate(_:)` — no `didStartProvisionalNavigation`, no `didCommit`, no `didFail`/`didFailProvisionalNavigation`, no `didFinish`. It arrives within a second, long before the budget.

Same command with the sandbox disabled:

    PROBE didStartProvisionalNavigation
    PROBE didCommit
    PROBE didFinish
    {…facts…}  EXIT=0

So the signal is a delegate/API one and stderr is never parsed. Note the stderr line names launchservicesd, but the *denial that matters* is the WebContent XPC service: a `sandbox-exec` profile that denies only `mach-lookup (global-name "com.apple.coreservices.launchservicesd")` still loads the page fine (it only logs an `_LSModifyNotification` failure); denying only `mach-lookup (global-name "com.apple.WebKit.WebContent")` reproduces the failure exactly. Anyone chasing this later should not grep for the launchservicesd string.

After the fix, same sandboxed command: exit 4, immediately, with

    WebKit could not start under this sandbox: its web content process was gone before file:///…/static.html began loading. Run the command outside the sandbox — in Claude Code, set dangerouslyDisableSandbox on that one Bash call, or allow WebKit with /sandbox.

## What changed

- New `Sources/SleepyHollow/Host/WebContentProcessFailure.swift`: public `Friendly` enum, `.neverLaunched` / `.crashedMidLoad`, with `error(url:)` producing the `SleepyError`. The observation above is recorded in its DocC.
- `PageHost`: new outcome case `.contentProcessEnded(WebContentProcessFailure)`; `hasStartedNavigation` set from the delegate; public `reportContentProcessTermination()` (classifies) and `reportContentProcessTermination(_:)` (the test seam); public `contentProcessFailure` so `sleepy doctor` (qixC5) can ask "can WebKit start here?" without reading an error string — load anything, then read that property.
- `PageHostDelegate`: added `didStartProvisionalNavigation`, `didCommit`, `webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate`.

A content process that dies *after* the navigation started is classified `.crashedMidLoad` and also reported as exit 4 rather than being left to time out — same "never a plausible wrong answer" ruling, one line of extra code.

## Tests

- `Tests/SleepyHollowTests/WebContentProcessFailureTests.swift` (new suite, 3 tests, no WebKit).
- `Tests/SleepyHollowTests/PageHostLoadTests.swift`: 3 new tests (seam through the real load pipeline; classification with no navigation; classification after a commit) plus an added assertion that a genuinely slow page leaves `contentProcessFailure == nil` and still exits 3.
- `Tests/SleepyGoldenTests/SandboxDenialGoldenTests.swift` (new suite): runs the real binary under `sandbox-exec` with a one-line profile denying `com.apple.WebKit.WebContent`, against `about:blank` (no fixture server needed), and asserts exit 4 + the message + the absence of "did not finish loading". Ran 4x standalone, 0.6–2.9s, no flakes. Skips itself if `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` is absent.

eval no longer answers `null` to a bare expression, and takes `--file`.

The decision is a typed value in the library
- `EvalOperation.SourceShape` (nested, `Friendly`): `.functionBody` (contains a `return` statement), `.expression` (no return, no `;`, non-empty — wrapped as `return (…);`), `.unreturnedStatements` (everything else, including empty — refused with a usage error, exit 2, naming the fix and repeating the async-function-body line).
- `EvalOperation.shape(of:)` is pure and `EvalOperation.evaluatedSource()` does the wrap-or-refuse; `execute(on:)` calls it before touching WebKit, so most of the coverage is unit tests with no page.
- The old DocC paragraph "Nothing is auto-wrapped … guessing … is how a tool starts returning silently wrong answers" is replaced by the new rule and why it is still safe: an expression with neither a `;` nor a `return` cannot be a statement list, so there is nothing to guess.

The `return` scan is stricter than `\breturn\b`, deliberately
A naive substring test makes `document.querySelector('[data-return]')` look like a function body — it would then run unwrapped and answer `null`, which is the exact bug this leaf fixes. So `return` counts only in statement position: nothing but spaces/tabs before it on its line, or an immediately preceding `;`, `{`, `}` or `)`, and no identifier character after it. `form.returnValue`, `returned` and `[data-return]` are expressions; `if (ready) return 1;`, `{ return 1; }` and a newline-separated `return` are bodies. Hand-rolled rather than Swift Regex because the package floor is macOS 12 (see the new gotchas.md entry).

The residual imprecision is one-way: a `;` inside a string literal costs the caller an explicit `return`, i.e. a refusal, never a wrong answer.

`--file`
`--js` is now optional and `--file <path>` reads a script from disk, `--file -` from stdin. Exactly one of the two: both, or neither, is exit 2 with a message naming the other flag. THE BRIEF'S DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG, AND SO WAS THE ORIGINAL BUG REPORT.

`--fill` IS a `shot` flag. It comes from the shared LoadFlagOptions group — the
ordered one-shot action flags --click/--fill/--submit that every loading verb
carries — and `sleepy shot --help` lists it. It is not "a different subcommand's
name leaking into the suggester".

And the suggester was already constrained to the invoked verb. Verified against
the built binary, not by reading:
  sleepy shot --sesion x  -> "Did you mean '--session'?"   (a shot flag)
  sleepy shot --selectr x -> no suggestion at all          (--selector is
                             query's; shot has none, so nothing is proposed)
The code is ArgumentParser's own UsageGenerator.unknownOptionMessage, which
filters its command's ArgumentSet by edit distance < 4. Our ErrorRendering
suggester (nearestVerb) never runs here: SleepyCommand.unknownVerb() returns nil
because "shot" IS a verb, so the failure goes straight to renderParsingFailure,
which passes ArgumentParser's text through verbatim.

So criterion QzO was already true before this leaf. There was nothing to
constrain and no code change was warranted for it. What I did instead:

1. Locked it. Tests/SleepyGoldenTests/ShotGoldenTests.swift now runs eight
   mistyped-flag invocations across shot/query/load/pdf, pulls any
   "Did you mean '--x'?" out of stderr with a regex, and asserts --x appears in

Follow-up: coordinator ruling adopted — a lone trailing `;` no longer refuses.

`SourceShape` now reads three lexical signals instead of two:
1. a `return` in statement position -> .functionBody (unchanged);
2. the body with one trailing `;` stripped: if what remains still contains a `;`, or is empty -> .unreturnedStatements;
3. if that remainder's leading word is a keyword that can only open a statement -> .unreturnedStatements; otherwise .expression, wrapped as `return (<remainder>);`.

So `document.querySelector('#save').click();` runs and prints `null` exit 0 — the call's own value, not a guess — while `const n = 1; document.title;` still exits 2.

Signal 3 is an addition to the ruling, not a contradiction of it. Without it, `const unused = 1;` has exactly the ruled shape (one trailing `;`) and would be wrapped into `return (const unused = 1);` — a page-side *syntax error*, exit 2 with WebKit's complaint instead of the teaching message. Refusing it up front strictly dominates: same exit code, better message, and no input that could have produced a value is affected, because a statement keyword cannot open an expression. The list is const/let/var/if/for/while/do/switch/try/throw/break/continue/debugger; `function` and `class` are deliberately absent, since `return (function () {})` is valid. The check is on the leading identifier-shaped word, so `constant.value;` is still an expression.

Tests: `a single trailing semicolon still reads as an expression` and `a trailing semicolon is dropped before wrapping` were written red and failed on exactly the ruled cases; the golden `a call with a trailing semicolon runs and answers its value` (a disabled `#publish` click -> null exit 0, and `chip.reportStatus();` -> "ready") failed on all four assertions before the change. `a script opening with a statement keyword is refused rather than wrapped` was partly green when written (its `const`/`throw` cases already passed) — it is a guard against the softening over-reaching, not a red test, and only its `constant.value;` case was red.

One existing test of mine changed: `statements with no return are refused, naming the fix` used `document.querySelector('h1').click();`, which the ruling makes legal; its probe is now an interior-`;` script.

DocC on `SourceShape`, the `EvalOperation` type comment, the refusal message and the `eval --help` paragraph all state the trailing-`;` rule. swiftformat lint clean; full suite 525 tests in 81 suites passed.

Edited: AGENTS.md docs list (+1 line), project/gotchas.md (rAF entry corrected in place; new #expect/CGFloat entry), PageHost.swift (+4 lines at 106: doc comment + `var offscreenWindow: OffscreenWindow?`, right after `hasImportedJar`).

THE HEADLINE, AND IT CONTRADICTS THE BRIEF'S PREMISE: a window is necessary but NOT sufficient. An off-screen NSWindow on its own does not make WebKit render — rAF stays frozen, CSS transitions do not advance, document.visibilityState stays "hidden" — at EVERY ordering (unordered / orderBack / orderFrontRegardless), and also for an on-screen alpha-0 window ordered front, with finishLaunching(), with the AppKit run loop pumped, and under the .accessory policy. In all of those `window.occlusionState` never contains `.visible`, which is what WKWebView derives page visibility from, and the window server will never call a window parked off every display visible.

What works is the window PLUS `-[WKWebView _setWindowOcclusionDetectionEnabled:]` = NO — private SPI, the same lever WebKit's own test runner pulls. With it: rAF 12 ticks/300ms (34/500ms idle, 4/500ms under the full suite — contended, never assert a rate), a 6s linear transition reads opacity 0.053167 after 319ms where the wall clock predicts 0.053167 (exact), visibilityState "visible". Shipped as `OffscreenWindow.Rendering.live` (default), isolated in one private func, guarded by responds(to:) so a future macOS degrades to `.hidden` and the rAF test goes red rather than lying. **This needs the main thread's ratification — it is the project's first private API.** Reverting is deleting one function and one `if`.

Ordering: measured irrelevant to rendering; it moves only NSWindow.isVisible. Default `Ordering.back` (least intrusive that still puts the window in the list, so isVisible is true for the AppKit printing paths 25Mev will use). 25Mev should confirm what NSPrintOperation actually needs — I did not measure printing.

DENSITY, for --scale: `wantsLayer` + `layer.contentsScale = 1 or 3` on the web view AND the content view changes NOTHING — devicePixelRatio stays 2 and the raw takeSnapshot raster stays 2560x1600 for a 1280x800 view. So option 1 of project/2026-08-28-shot-scale-flag.md ("force the source density with contentsScale") does not work as written; the doc records that. `-[WKWebView _setOverrideDeviceScaleFactor:]` DOES move devicePixelRatio (1 or 3) with innerWidth unchanged at 1280 — the right page-side semantics — but the raw snapshot raster still came back 2560x1600 in every case, i.e. host-screen scale. Whether a 1x host can be made to emit 2x pixels is unanswered; the honest fallback stays "refuse rather than fake it".

Nothing visible is proved during a real load+snapshot: window.screen == nil, frame intersects no NSScreen, every *visible* NSApp window is off every screen, NSApp.isActive == false, activationPolicy == .prohibited (set once, before the first window). Note the first draft asserted over ALL NSApp.windows and failed on a 500x500 TUINSWindow the test host owns — hence "visible" in the filter.

Gotcha found and isolated: `#expect(aDouble == aCGFloat)` FAILS even when both are 2.0 (plain Swift `==` on the same values is true). Cost me a confusing red. Recorded in gotchas.md.

Suite-load care: each probe holds a WebKitGate slot while it sleeps, so the probe window is 300ms and every assertion is qualitative (frozen vs running). One full-suite run mid-development showed two WaitPredicateTests budget flakes; the four runs since (with the shorter probe) were clean.

**Files**
- `Sources/SleepyHollow/Operations/ShotGrid.swift` (180 lines) — the namespace: `Mode` (`.rulersAndLines` = "lines", `.rulers`, plus `init(parsing:)` for the CLI), `Options(mode:step:)` (step default 100), `Tick(cssPosition:pixelOffset:)` with a `label`, `Layout(for:options:pixelsPerCSSPixel:)` (gutter widths + both rulers' ticks), and the pure `ticks(fromCSSOrigin:acrossPixels:pixelsPerCSSPixel:step:)`.
- `Sources/SleepyHollow/Operations/ShotGrid+Draw.swift` (238 lines) — `draw(_:on:pixelsPerCSSPixel:) throws -> ShotCapture`, the in-page lines, the ruler marks, Core Text labels, colours. Split out because one file was 406 lines, over the Swift section's ~300 ceiling.
- `Tests/SleepyHollowTests/ShotGridTests.swift` — 12 unit tests over synthetic CGImages, no WebKit.

**Design decisions worth reviewing**
1. *Density is an explicit argument, not `ShotCapture.scale`.* `draw` and `Layout` take `pixelsPerCSSPixel: CGFloat`, so the stage composes with whatever the `--max-size` fit stage arrives at (0.37 px/CSS px is a legitimate input) as well as with an unfitted `--scale 2`. Called out in DocC on the type.
2. *The result keeps the input's `rect` and `scale`.* The gutter is chrome, not content — the pixels still show exactly that document rect — so a gridded capture's `pixelSize` is deliberately larger than `rect x scale`. Documented on `draw`.
3. *The left gutter is adaptive*: `max(24, widest row label + 2*3)`. A 24 px fixed gutter clips a 5-digit label ("12000" is ~27 px at 9 pt SF Mono), and a clipped ruler label is exactly the "plausible wrong answer" the synthesis doc rules out. The top gutter stays 24.
4. *Labels are suppressed where they would collide* (a fit down to 0.1 px/CSS px puts step ticks 10 px apart). Ticks are still drawn at every step; only the numbers thin out. Deterministic, no random sampling.
5. *In-page lines are mid-gray at alpha 0.35*, not a black or white tint, so they read over a dark-theme page as well as a white one.
6. *Byte-identity mechanics*: the page is blitted at an integer offset with `CGBlendMode.copy`, `interpolationQuality = .none`, antialiasing off for every rect fill; ruler marks live wholly inside the gutter; label text is drawn under a clip rect that excludes the page area, with `setShouldSmoothFonts(false)` and subpixel positioning/quantization off. Verified byte-for-byte, not merely by eye.

**Verification**
- `swiftformat . --lint --config .swiftformat` in the worktree: 0/245 need formatting.
- `swift test --quiet`: 572 tests in 89 suites passed (34s), sandbox off.
- Red first: the 12 tests failed to compile ("cannot find 'ShotGrid' in scope") before the implementation. One test then failed on my own faulty expectation (I asserted a neighbouring page *row* was unchanged in lines mode, forgetting the vertical column lines cross every row) — rewritten to assert three specific pixels: on a row line, on a column line, and on neither.
- Eyeballed a real render (a blue box on white, `--rect 0,850,840,600` at 0.5 px/CSS px): top ruler reads 0..800, left ruler 900..1400, box lands where the labels say. Scratch render test deleted afterwards.

The named case is `ticks(fromCSSOrigin: 850, acrossPixels: 120, pixelsPerCSSPixel: 0.5, step: 100)` -> first tick cssPosition 900, pixelOffset 25 — not 50, not 100. Also covered: origin on a step boundary (tick 0), a fitted 0.25 density (137 -> first label 200 at 15.75 px), and a `--scale 2` capture (labels 0/100/200 at 0/200/400 px).

`click --at x,y` ships: a real hit test that descends open shadow roots.

**Coordinate space, settled: document CSS px** — page top-left is 0,0, unscrolled, the same
space `shot --rect` crops in and the coming `--grid` labels report, so a measured number pastes
across without conversion. One space, no flag. The verb scrolls the point into view itself and
hit-tests at the viewport-relative position (`elementFromPoint` takes nothing else); a point past
the end of the document is a clean negative rather than a click at the clamped scroll offset.
Recorded as a marked block quote in `project/2026-08-28-agent-feedback-synthesis.md`, which had
left it as "viewport or document CSS px".

**Mechanism.** `document.elementFromPoint` stops at the shadow *host* — that is the outermost
node in the document's own tree — so the resolver then calls `shadowRoot.elementFromPoint` at the
same coordinates, repeatedly, while the element it lands on has an open `shadowRoot` (cap 32).
The click is dispatched at the point, not at the element's centre, through the same
pointerdown/mousedown/pointerup/mouseup/click sequence a selector click uses (factored out as
`sleepyDispatchClick`, so the two can never drift). A closed root exposes no `shadowRoot` to
anyone, this tool included: the descent stops at its host, and `--help` says so rather than
implying it pierced.

**Typing.** `ActionTarget` (`.selector` | `.point(DocumentPoint)`) replaces the selector string on
`ClickOperation` and on the `ActionScript` seam — one enum, not two optionals, and
`ActionTarget.clicking(selector:at:)` holds the exclusivity decision in the library so the CLI
wires nothing. `ActionOutcome.selector` is now optional (nil for a point: naming a plausible
selector that could not have reached the element would be exactly the wrong answer) and a new
`hit: HitElement?` reports tag, id, classes, `shadowDepth` and the point. The refusal vocabulary
moved to `ActionScript+Failures.swift` with two new codes, `no-hit` and `off-page`.

**Tests.** `ClickPointTests` proves the pair the field report asked about: a click at the button's
coordinates activates it (`document.title`/`data-activated` both change), and `--selector '#panel'`
on its host does *not* — same fixture, same page, one line apart. Plus the outcome's hit fields,
the bare-`<body>` negative, the past-the-document negative, and a document-space check on a panel
1300px down that only passes if the verb scrolled. `ActionTargetTests` covers the parse and the
exclusivity without WebKit; four goldens cover the CLI's exit 2s and the help's coordinate-space
claim. Smoke-tested over a real session end to end (open → eval-measure → click --at → title).

**Found, not fixed — someone should reconcile this.** `ShotRegion`'s DocC says document CSS px is
"the coordinate system every other verb reports in", but `ElementFact.Geometry` is
`getBoundingClientRect` with no scroll added: `query` reports **viewport** space. The two agree
only on an unscrolled page — which every one-shot load is, and which a session stops being the
moment anything scrolls it, including a previous `click --at`. I did not change `query`
(cross-cutting, and not this leaf's call); instead `click --help` states the difference and tells
the agent to add `window.scrollX/scrollY`. Worth a leaf: either `query` reports document space, or
the convention doc stops claiming it does.

`sleepy doctor` built on wt/doctor. Four checks in a fixed order — binary,
webkit, sessions, temp — each a typed `DoctorCheck` (Kind, Status, detail,
nextMove?), rolled up in a `DoctorReport` that owns the verdict, the JSON
shape, the `--format text` rendering and the thrown error. The command is
thin: resolve format, `await Doctor.run(...)`, write the report, throw
`report.error`. Report goes to stdout even on failure, then the first failure
lands on stderr with exit 5 — the whole diagnosis and the headline both.

New library files: Core/DoctorCheck.swift, Core/DoctorReport.swift,
Host/Doctor.swift. New CLI file: sleepy/DoctorCommand.swift. Every check is
separately callable and takes its subject as a parameter, so both the pass
and the fail are proved without a subprocess.

The webkit check reuses `WebContentProcessFailure.error(url:)` verbatim
rather than restating it, so `doctor` and a denied `load` say the same words.
Every failure is mapped to `.environment` (exit 5) whatever the underlying
kind — doctor only ever asks environment questions.

Criterion 8pq is proved by DoctorGoldenTests, using the sandbox-exec profile
extracted from SandboxDenialGoldenTests into a shared SandboxedBinary helper
(the old suite now calls it; the profile and runner had to be shared, and
duplicating 30 lines was the alternative). The test decodes the report and
asserts the denial is pinned to WebKit: exit 5, the sandbox message and
`dangerouslyDisableSandbox` on stderr, and the other three checks still ok.
Also verified by hand: the built binary run inside this agent's own Bash
sandbox exits 5 with that text; run with the sandbox off it exits 0 with
every check ok.

Two findings worth keeping.

1. The temp check first shipped with the next move "Set TMPDIR to a directory
   you can write". That is wrong. A `swiftc` probe run inside Claude Code's
   Bash sandbox (with TMPDIR=/tmp/claude-501 exported) showed BOTH
   `NSTemporaryDirectory()` and `FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory`
   still answering /var/folders/rl/…/T — Foundation resolves the temp
   directory itself on Darwin and ignores the variable. So the advice would
   have been a plausible instruction that changes nothing, exactly the
   failure the feedback synthesis rules out. The next move now says to run
   outside the sandbox or allow writes to that directory, a test pins that it
   never starts "Set TMPDIR", and Doctor's DocC records the measurement.

2. Nothing in Sources/ stages files in a temp directory — my first DocC for
   the check claimed screenshots and PDFs were staged there, which was false.
   Corrected: the check exists because WebKit, Foundation and any
   `--out $TMPDIR/…` an agent writes need it, not because sleepy does.
   Consequence worth knowing: inside Claude Code's Bash sandbox, `doctor`
   reports temp failed as well as webkit failed. Both are true.

sentence gained "; `sleepy doctor` when a call failed and you don't know why"
(ScaffoldGoldenTests' byte pin updated to match); a recipe line in

`shot --max-size <px>` caps the longest side of the output PNG; the page is
untouched. New stage `Sources/SleepyHollow/Operations/ShotFit.swift` — a
`Friendly` struct, pure over ShotCapture -> ShotCapture, downsampling through a
CGContext at `.high` interpolation. Its throwing init refuses a cap of 0 or

Expressing the fit: no new stored field on ShotCapture. `rect` stays the CSS
document rect and `scale` stays the *render* density (documented as such in
both ShotCapture and ShotImage); the new derived
`ShotCapture.pixelsPerCSSPixel` = image.width / rect.width is what a later
stage (grid labels, tile index) reads for "how much detail does this image
actually hold". Derived, so it cannot drift from the pixels.

- SleepyHelpers+Color.swift — colour parsing (rgb/rgba, comma or slash syntax,
  percentage alpha, hex, `transparent`, SVG `none`), source-over compositing,
  WCAG relative luminance and contrast ratio, hex formatting.
- SleepyHelpers+Elements.swift — `sleepyRect`, `sleepyPath` (selector-ish, id

- SleepyHelpers+Contrast.swift / +Overflow.swift — the two computations.
- Sources/SleepyHollow/Operations/DocumentRect.swift — the shared rect struct

`effectiveBackground(el)` walks ancestors compositing translucent
`background-color` layers over an opaque-white canvas and returns
`{ kind: "color", rgba: [r,g,b,a] }`; at the first `background-image` (a
gradient counts) it returns `{ kind: "unknown", reason: "image" }` and stops.

Decision worth flagging: the canvas beneath everything is assumed **opaque
white**. There is no API for the backdrop a headless WKWebView actually paints,
and white is what it paints when no page rule says otherwise. Documented in the
file. If `--theme dark` ever changes that backdrop this assumption needs

`ContrastMinimum` is an enum — `.wcagAA`, `.wcagAAA`, `.ratio(Double)` — with
`normalThreshold`/`largeThreshold`, so the two-bar nature of WCAG is in the type
rather than in a comment. It encodes as the single string it is typed as, so the
JSON reads `"minimum": "wcag-aa"`.

Design decisions worth review:

1. **Unmeasured is its own list, and does not exit 1.** Text over a
   `background-image` lands in `unmeasured` with `ratio: null`, `background:
   null`, `reason: "image"`. A gap is not a proven failure, so it does not flip
   the exit code — but both the JSON and the text form print it, and the help
   says so under Exit codes. If the intent was "unknown means exit 1", that is
   a one-line change in `ContrastReport.passes`.
2. **A `--selector` that matches nothing is exit 2, not a clean pass.** The JS
   reports `scopeMatches`; the operation throws usage when the selector was
   given and matched zero. An empty scope passing with `checked: 0` is exactly
   the plausible-wrong-answer the synthesis doc rules out.
3. **Large text** is WCAG's own rule in CSS px: >=24px, or >=18.66px with
   computed weight >=700. The ratio is rounded to two places *before*
   comparison, the way conformance tools quote it, so 3.00 meets a 3.0 bar.
4. **SVG background** is the topmost shape (path/rect/circle/ellipse/polygon/
   polyline) whose fill covers all five of the text's corner+centre points,
   found with `getScreenCTM().inverse()` + `isPointInFill`, then composited over
   whatever the ordinary ancestor walk finds beneath the `<svg>`. Foreground for
   SVG text is computed `fill` (with `fill-opacity`), not `color`.

`pdf` rebuilt on the print path. Measurements, and the two places the brief was wrong.

ORDERING / RENDERING (the open question in project/2026-08-28-offscreen-window-host.md)
Measured all six (Ordering, Rendering) pairs against print-paginated.html at Letter: every one produced byte-identical output — 15,207 bytes, 5 pages, body text present, .no-print absent. Ordering does not matter; Rendering does not matter, so `pdf` never touches the private occlusion selector. The control: a web view in NO window, printed modally for an unrelated off-screen window hosting a plain NSView, produced the same 15,207 bytes and 5 pages. What needs a window is `runModal(for:)`, whose parameter is a window — not the view. PDFOperation therefore asks for ensureOffscreenWindow(ordering: .unordered, rendering: .hidden): least intrusive, never in the window list, no SPI. OffscreenWindow's own defaults (.back, .live) are untouched; ensureOffscreenWindow grew default arguments instead.

Recorded as a dated addendum in project/2026-08-28-offscreen-window-host.md, with a block-quote correction on section (d), whose claim that `.back` was needed "so NSWindow.isVisible is true for the AppKit printing paths" is now measured false.

NSPrintOperation(view:) IS THE WRONG CONSTRUCTOR
The brief (and the field report) specified NSPrintOperation(view: webView, printInfo:). It paginates correctly and draws NOTHING: 5 Letter sheets whose PDFDocument.string is "". The page is in another process, so AppKit's drawing pass has no content. WKWebView.printOperation(with:) — public, macOS 11+, above our macOS 12 floor — is the only path that emits text. That is almost certainly the same defect behind the field report's "infinite empty pages": empty is what this constructor produces.

didRun: ARRIVES ON A BACKGROUND THREAD
runModal(for:delegate:didRun:contextInfo:) completes on a secondary NSThread (-[NSConcretePrintOperation _continueModalOperationToTheEnd:]). An @objc callback that inherits @MainActor isolation from its class dies in swift_task_checkIsolated: EXC_BREAKPOINT, exit 133, and NO "Fatal error:" line anywhere in swift test's output. Only the crash report in ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports names it. PrintRunner's callback is nonisolated and hops back; the selector is pinned with @objc(printOperationDidRun:success:contextInfo:) so the formatter's unusedArguments rewrite cannot move it. Added to project/gotchas.md.

MARGINS: THE PAGE WINS, OUTRIGHT
First-page text bounding box relative to the media box (PDFPage.selection(for: mediaBox) then PDFSelection.bounds(for:)):

  no @page rule,          NSPrintInfo 0pt  -> 5 pages, inset left 0.0,  top 3.7
  no @page rule,          NSPrintInfo 72pt -> 6 pages, inset left 72.0, top 75.7
  @page { margin:1.25in}, NSPrintInfo 0pt  -> 3 pages, inset left 90.0, top 93.7
  @page { margin:1.25in}, NSPrintInfo 72pt -> 3 pages, inset left 90.0, top 93.7

A @page rule REPLACES the NSPrintInfo margin rather than adding to it; a document with no rule takes the NSPrintInfo value. So our number only decides what an unstyled page gets. Ruling: all four NSPrintInfo margins are zero, stated in DocC and in `sleepy pdf --help`. The rule a caller learns is one sentence — the page decides the margins — with no inset a stylesheet cannot see or cancel. Cost: a page with no @page rule prints edge to edge; the fix is one line of CSS. `--margin <pt>` was NOT built (it would be a second way to say what CSS already says, and could only ever affect pages that said nothing); what would un-park it is real pages that need margins and cannot be edited.

WHAT LANDED
Sources/SleepyHollow/Operations/PDFOperation.swift (rebuilt), PrintRunner.swift (new), PaperSize.swift (new, letter/a4), Sources/SleepyCLIKit/PaperSize+ExpressibleByArgument.swift (new), Sources/sleepy/PdfCommand.swift (--paper, help rewritten), Sources/SleepyHollow/Host/PageHost+Window.swift (ensureOffscreenWindow gained ordering:/rendering: default arguments). FOR THE INTEGRATOR (files I was told not to edit)
- OffscreenWindow.swift DocC says "NSPrintOperation, which pdf pagination needs, refuses a view that has none." Measured false — see above. Suggested rewording: it is runModal(for:) that needs a window; the printed view need not be in one.

Unrelated to this leaf (shot's path is untouched), passed in isolation and on two later full runs. Pre-existing contention flake.

data.text:
Geometry space unified on **document CSS px**: `getBoundingClientRect()` + `window.scrollX/scrollY`. A rect from `query` now pastes into `shot --rect` and its centre into `click --at` at any scroll position.

## Audit: every geometry source

| source | space before | space after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `query` — `ElementFact.Geometry` (QueryOperation JS) | **viewport** CSS px (bare `getBoundingClientRect`) | **document** CSS px (`+ window.scrollX/scrollY`) — the fix |
| `shot --element` — `ShotOperation.boundingRect(of:on:)` | client rect measured on the grown frame: document *by accident* vertically, off by `scrollX` horizontally — but consistent with the snapshot rect, so the crop itself was right | document, on purpose: `resetScroll(on:)` puts the page at 0,0 after the frame grows, so view space **is** document space |
| `shot --rect` — `ShotRegion.rect` → `WKSnapshotConfiguration.rect` | document only while `scrollX == 0`; a horizontally scrolled page cropped the wrong columns | document at any scroll (same `resetScroll`) |
| `ShotImage.rect` (what a tile/grid index reports) | view rect; document only when unscrolled | always document |
| `click --at` — `DocumentPoint`, `HitElement.point`, `ActionScript+HitTest` | document (converts to viewport itself for `elementFromPoint`) | unchanged — this was the reference |
| `sleepy.rect` / `sleepyRectOf` (SleepyHelpers+Elements) | document already (`box.left + window.scrollX`) | unchanged |
| `overflow` — `OverflowReport.Violation.rect` (`DocumentRect`, via `sleepyRectOf`) | document | unchanged |
| `find` (FindOperation) | reports no geometry at all — `Bool` | unchanged |
| `ax` (AXNode / AXScript), `dom` (DOMNode), `style` (StyleResult) | report no geometry at all | unchanged |
| `click --selector` centre (ActionScript+Bodies) | viewport — internal only, never reported; `dispatchEvent` client coords must be viewport | unchanged, correct as is |
| SVG background hit-test (SleepyHelpers+Contrast, `getScreenCTM`/`isPointInFill`) | viewport — internal only, never reported; `getScreenCTM` is viewport space | unchanged, correct as is |

## Measured

Growing the web view frame to `document.documentElement.scrollHeight` collapses the vertical scroll range, and WebKit clamps `scrollY` to 0 by the next JS evaluation (probe on `capture-tall.html`: `scrollTo(0,1500)` → after grow `[scrollY 0, innerHeight 3016, #target.top 2400]`). `scrollX` is **not** clamped — the frame width is never grown — which is the horizontal `--rect` bug above. The page is also left at scroll 0 after the frame is restored; that was already true before this leaf, and now costs nothing observable, because no reported coordinate depends on where the page sits.

## Not done, on purpose

- **No `scrollX`/`scrollY` in the `query` output.** `QueryOperation.Output` is `[ElementFact]` — a bare array with no page-level facts object — so adding them means reshaping the wire type and the `--format text` renderer for a number that `sleepy eval <page> 'return [window.scrollX, window.scrollY]'` already returns. Documented that recovery in `ElementFact.Geometry`'s DocC instead.
- **`overflow`'s `rect.x + rect.width > viewportWidth` comparison** measures a document-space right edge against a viewport width, so it assumes `scrollX == 0`. Pre-existing, outside this leaf, and not reached by any current test — flagged, not touched.

## Files

- `Sources/SleepyHollow/Operations/QueryOperation.swift` — the JS fix + DocC
- `Sources/SleepyHollow/Operations/ElementFact.swift` — `Geometry` DocC now says document space and how to get back to viewport space
- `Sources/SleepyHollow/Operations/ShotOperation.swift` — `resetScroll(on:)` before measuring any non-viewport region
- `Sources/SleepyHollow/Operations/ShotRegion.swift`, `DocumentRect.swift` — DocC claims made true
- `Sources/sleepy/ClickCommand.swift` — the "add window.scrollX/scrollY" caveat removed from `--at`'s discussion
- `Sources/sleepy/QueryCommand.swift` — one line of help teaching the space
- `Tests/SleepyHollowTests/GeometrySpaceTests.swift` (new, 5 tests, all red first)
- `Tests/TestSupport/Fixtures/capture-wide.html` (new — a 2400×3000 page, `#target` at 900,2400 300×200, for the horizontal-scroll cases)
- `project/2026-08-28-agent-feedback-synthesis.md` — the "not fixed here" caveat closed as a dated block quote

Suite: `swift test --quiet` → 705 tests in 106 suites passed. `swiftformat . --lint --config .swiftformat` → clean.

Success nudges landed on branch wt/teach (worktree .claude/worktrees/teach).

WHAT SHIPPED

- `Sources/SleepyCLIKit/Nudge.swift` — a typed `Nudge: Friendly` enum. Two cases, each
  carrying its trigger facts and knowing its own text:
  - `.captureTallerThanVisionBudget(cssHeight: Int)`
  - `.baselineComparisonIsImageWork`
  `Nudge.visionBudgetCSSPixels = 2000` is the one named constant.
  `Nudge.forShot(ShotFacts)` is the selector: it returns *at most one* tip, priority-ordered
  (an unreadable image is a wasted call; a missing baseline is only a missed convenience,
  so the readout tip wins when both apply). `Nudge.emit(_:quiet:to:)` is the single writer —
  stderr, one line, nothing when quiet or when the tip is nil. A future tip is a case plus a
  line in `forShot` (or a sibling `for…` selector), never a new stderr call in a command.
  `ShotFacts` is a nested struct (captureHeight/wasCapped/wasTiled/wroteToFile) so the command
  hands over observations and every rule about which tip they justify stays in one place.

- `Sources/SleepyCLIKit/Options/QuietOption.swift` — the global `--quiet` flag.

- `Sources/sleepy/ShotCommand.swift` — `@OptionGroup var quiet: QuietOption` plus ONE
  `Nudge.emit(...)` call at the end of `run()`, past every throw (so a failed call never
  nudges) and past the writes (so success is real).

- `Sources/sleepy/SleepyCommand.swift` — the pending primer sentence appended to the Help line:
  "Comparing a render against a saved baseline is image work, not page work: `peep compare`
  (PixelPeeper) does it." The byte pin in `Tests/SleepyGoldenTests/ScaffoldGoldenTests.swift`
  moved with it, and `HelpGoldenTests` gained
  `the primer names peep compare for baselines`.

WHERE --quiet LIVES, AND WHY

Its own `QuietOption` group, adopted by every visible verb — not a field on `OutOption`.
`OutOption` answers "where does the artifact go"; `--quiet` answers "does the tool volunteer
advice", and five verbs that take no `--out` (`close`, `recipes`, `jars clear`, `jars rm`,
`sessions close`) still have to accept it. A flag an agent can type on one verb and not the
next is exactly the inconsistency this epic exists to remove. Hidden `_host` is excluded on
purpose. `NudgeGoldenTests.verbsAcceptingQuiet` is the checklist, asserted through `--help`.

TIP TEXTS

- "Tip: a 12,982-px capture is more than a vision model reads well; --max-size 2000 gives an
  overview, --tile strips at readable scale."
- "Tip: comparing a render against a saved baseline is image work, not page work — write this
  one with --out, then `peep compare` (PixelPeeper) diffs the two."

The height is grouped by a hand-rolled `grouped(_:)`, not `NumberFormatter`: a formatter's
grouping separator follows the host locale, and a tip whose bytes change with the machine
that printed it is not determinism by construction.

DEVIATIONS FROM THE BRIEF

1. ONE call site, not two. The brief said "the two nudge call sites"; a single
