data.text:
Diagnosed and fixed at the source: the three tests each bet that the *host*
gets back to the page before a page-side `setTimeout` fires, and under
parallel-agent load the host stretches 20-50x while page timers keep wall
time. Full write-up with figures: project/2026-08-28-wait-test-timing.md.

MEASURED (throwaway probe test, now deleted; fixture marker
`window.sleepyLoadAt` in wait-late.html stayed). Quiet: `PageHost.load` of a
local fixture 108-147 ms (first load in a process 1804 ms, WebKit warm-up).
Under the full 700-test suite plus twelve `yes` spinners on 8 cores: the
page-clock gap from the load event to the host's first `evaluate` was 153,
205, 231, 302, 696, 1149 ms, and `load()` itself 1677-7019 ms for the same
trivial page. A full suite that runs in 47 s unloaded took 742 s under
sixteen spinners.

PER TEST

1. "wait load still settles on the load event alone" - `#late` is appended by
   a 3000 ms page timer started at parse; the test asserted it absent after
   `load()` returned. That holds only while host latency from parse to the
   first evaluate stays under 3 s - measured at 1.1 s under load with `load()`
   alone reaching 7 s. REPRODUCED, forced: the same assertion with its margin
   at 200 ms failed in a loaded full-suite run with the exact reported
   wording, `Expectation failed: (matched -> "true") == "false"`.

2. "a selector already present when the load event fires settles at once" -
   same fixture, same 3000 ms flip, assertion one evaluation later (after
   facts.httpStatus), so strictly less margin than #1. Same forced
   reproduction covers it.

3. "a slow navigation leaves the wait less budget, not a fresh one" - budget
   1 s, document delayed 900 ms, `#late` at parse+300 ms, expecting a
   timeout. Two host clocks decide it: `PageHost.navigate`'s budget task
   (`Task.sleep(1s)` resumed on the main actor) and WebKit's `didFinish`.
   When main-actor congestion delays the budget task past a `didFinish` that
   is itself late - reachable when the first load in a process costs 1.7 s
   against a 1 s budget - `navigate` returns `.finished` after the deadline
   has already passed, and `WaitEngine.settleSelector` takes its first probe
   *before* consulting the deadline, finds `#late` already in the DOM (the
   page's 300 ms timer fired on time long ago) and returns success. No
   timeout, so `Issue.record("expected a timeout")` fires. NOT REPRODUCED:
   this is the only mechanism consistent with the failure and the numbers
   make it reachable, but I never caught it red.

FIX - route (1), ordering instead of elapsed time. New
`TestSupport/FixtureGate.swift`: a latch registered as a server route that
holds every request until the test calls `open()`. `wait-late.html?flip=gate`
appends `#late` when that request resolves (a `fetch`, deliberately - an
outstanding fetch does not delay the load event, a script or image element
would). With the gate closed the page *cannot* have flipped, so "the element
is not there yet" is program order, not a race. Applied to #1, #2, the
identical untouched twin in WaitPredicateTests ("a predicate already true at
the load event settles at once" - same fixture, same 3000 ms bet, not yet
flaked but the same bug), plus two generously bounded liveness checks so the
assertions cannot pass vacuously.

#3 keeps one timing element, because "the wait got less than a fresh budget"
is irreducibly about elapsed time, but it is now one-sided and anchored to
the page: the release waits for the page's own gate request (which happens at
parse, i.e. when the navigation's delay is spent) and then sleeps
`budget - delay + 0.5s`. That lands after the shared deadline and inside the
fresh per-phase deadline a regression would grant, with both margins moving
with the navigation however slow it was. A sleep can only fire late, so a
loaded machine can only push the release past both deadlines and make the
test prove less - it can never end the wait early and turn it red.

NOT DONE: route (2), an injectable clock. The fragile quantity is not the
engine's cadence but the skew between the page's real `setTimeout` and the
host's scheduling; a fake clock removes neither, so it would move the flake
rather than end it, and `deadline` is a `DispatchTime` threaded from
`PageHost` through the navigate budget task, `runActionSteps` and the engine -
a broad change to PageHost for no gain here. Route (3) was rejected as the
fix; the bounds that remain (15 s "the page reached the gate", 15 s "the
element arrived once opened") are pure liveness guards that decide nothing.

VERIFIED: the gated tests were green in the same loaded full-suite run in
which the old-style assertion went red, and green 4/4 in filtered runs under
twelve spinners. Full suite green twice on a quiet machine (700 tests, 47.4 s
and 58.5 s), `swiftformat . --lint --config .swiftformat` clean.

ALSO: `scripts/flake-hunt.sh` takes an optional spinner count
(`flake-hunt.sh <iterations> <spinners>`) so this load is reproducible -
SwiftPM's exclusive `.build` lock means a second `swift test` in the same
worktree proves nothing about contention. Two gotchas entries added (never
assert the host beat a page timer; use spinners not a second `swift test`),
and the 2026-08-20 WebKitGate entry corrected in place: it fixed the
wait-family *timeouts*, not the tests that raced a page timer.

Built on wt/shot2. `--scale 1|2|3`, default 1: device px per CSS px in the PNG, viewport and breakpoints untouched.

Shape: new `ShotScale` (Sources/SleepyHollow/Operations/ShotScale.swift) — a validating wrapper like `ShotFit`, 1...3, with `dotsPerInch = 72 * factor`. `ShotOperation.scale: ShotScale` (wire field; `init(region:scale:fit:tile:grid:)`). `render` reads the *source* density back from the snapshot NSImage's own bitmap rep (`ShotCapture.density(of:)` = pixelsWide / size.width) and refuses a denser request with `.environment` (exit 5) — "This host renders at 2×; --scale 3 would upsample." Never upsamples. Then `ShotCapture.rasterize(image, atPixelSize: rect.size * factor)`.

DPI: `ShotCapture.encoded()` now sets `bitmap.size = pixels / scale`, so the PNG carries 72 × scale dpi (measured: 144 at scale 2). At scale 1 NSBitmapImageRep writes no pHYs chunk at all, which every reader treats as 72 — the test helper reports the absent chunk as 72 and says so.

Brief said exit 4 then corrected itself to `.environment`/5; shipped as 5. The doc's "force the source density" option was already measured dead (offscreen-window-host § (c)) and was not attempted. `project/2026-08-28-shot-scale-flag.md` now carries a dated correction block over its Recommendation: option 1 dead, exit code 5, and `--scale` since became a sweep axis.

Grid labels stay in CSS px for free: `ShotOperation` passes `capture.pixelsPerCSSPixel` (= 2 at scale 2) to `ShotGrid`, so a tick at CSS 100 lands at pixel 200 and still reads "100". Asserted in ShotScaleTests.

Tests (red first, except where noted): Tests/SleepyHollowTests/ShotScaleTests.swift (validation, dpi, grid density), Tests/SleepyHollowTests/CaptureShotScaleTests.swift (8 WebKit cases), Tests/SleepyGoldenTests/ShotScaleGoldenTests.swift (5 CLI cases), fixture Tests/TestSupport/Fixtures/capture-breakpoint.html (blue at >=1000 CSS px, red below). The `--full-page` half of criterion 997 was added *after* the implementation and was green on its first run — it fills a coverage gap rather than driving code.

Measured on this 2x host: scale 2 succeeds, scale 3 exits 5. The scale-2 capture downsampled to 1280x800 differs from the scale-1 capture by a mean of <4/255 per channel (antialiasing only).

Repro: `sleepy shot <url> --size 1280x800 --scale 2 --out b.png`; `swift test --filter CaptureShotScaleTests`.

Closing criterion PLC on wt/shot2, now that `--scale` exists (leaf 5BKGq).

`--rect 0,850,1280,1285 --scale 2` yields exactly 2560×2570 and reports the same CSS rect back. Verified twice: at the operation level (Tests/SleepyHollowTests/CaptureShotScaleTests.swift, "a rect capture at scale 2 is exactly twice the scale-1 pixels", against capture-tall.html) and end to end through the binary (Tests/SleepyGoldenTests/ShotScaleGoldenTests.swift, "--rect 0,850,1280,1285 --scale 2 writes a 2560x2570 PNG", against capture-banded.html with --budget 60000).

Composition holds because the rect stays in CSS px through the whole pipeline: `ShotOperation.render` resolves the region to a document rect, then rasterizes at `rect.size × scale`, and `ShotCapture.rect` is never touched by a later stage. So `image.rect` after a scale-2 rect capture equals the rect the caller passed, and a tile index entry still pastes straight back.

No production code was needed for this leaf beyond 5BKGq's; the pre-carved `--rect` on main was already correct.

Built on wt/shot2. `--size`, `--scale` and `--theme` repeat; the cross product renders once per combination, files suffix only the axes that vary, and a JSON index lands on stdout.

Library: `ShotPlan` (Sources/SleepyHollow/Operations/ShotPlan.swift) holds the three axes and produces `Variant`s carrying size/scale/theme plus a precomputed `suffix` and human `label`. `ShotVariantIndex` (sibling of `ShotIndex`, not an extension of it) is the wire shape: `{ variants: [{ file, width, height, scale, theme }] }`.

Decisions made here, worth review:

1. **Where the repeatable form lives.** ArgumentParser cannot declare `--size` twice, so a shot-only option group was not possible. Instead `LoadFlagOptions.size`/`.theme` became `[String]`/`[ColorTheme]` (`parsing: .singleValue`) for *every* verb, and `resolveLoadOptions(steps:)` — which every other verb goes through — now **refuses** a repeat with a usage error naming `shot`. `shot` skips that refusal via a new `resolveLoadOptions(steps:size:theme:)` that supplies the pair for one combination. `PageExecution.perform` gained a `loadOptions:` parameter so the sweep can hand in its own; `PageExecution.actionSteps()` exposes the argv scan both paths need. `OpenCommand` calls `requireSingleRenderAxes()` up front so a repeat fails at `open` rather than inside the helper.

2. **Enumeration order is size → theme → scale, while the *suffix* order stays size, scale, theme.** Scale is raster-only, so variants differing only in density share one page load; putting scale innermost makes those adjacent and `ShotPlan.loads` groups them in one pass. A 2-size × 2-scale × 2-theme sweep therefore pays for 4 loads, not 8. Sizes and themes are `LoadOptions` facts and each pair gets its own `PageHost` load — no resize-and-flip on a live host, which would have to be measured before it could be trusted.

3. **Size suffix is the width alone (`-480`) unless two sizes share a width, in which case it is `-480x800`** — otherwise two renders would claim one file.

4. **A sweep requires a URL.** `--session` names one already-loaded page, so a sweep's index would report a size and theme the session never rendered. Refused with a usage error rather than reporting a plausible wrong answer. Cost: a scale-only sweep over a session, which nobody has asked for.

5. **A sweep refuses `--tile`.** Both claim the `--out` stem and stdout, and strips from four renders scramble the reading order the tile index exists to preserve.

Also fixed in passing: `--out` suffixing went through `URL(fileURLWithPath:)`, which absolutised a *relative* path, so `--tile --out strips.png` would have reported `/cwd/strips-01.png` in its index. Both the tile numbers and the sweep suffixes now go through `ShotPlan.suffixed`, which is string surgery.

Files: Sources/SleepyHollow/Operations/ShotPlan.swift, ShotVariantIndex.swift; Sources/sleepy/ShotCommand+Sweep.swift (new, keeps ShotCommand.swift readable); edits to LoadFlagOptions.swift, PageExecution.swift, OpenCommand.swift, ShotCommand.swift.

Tests (red first): ShotPlanTests.swift, ShotVariantIndexTests.swift, RenderAxisOptionTests.swift (width-only `--size 480`, repeats refused elsewhere, the session refusal still sees `--size`), ShotSweepGoldenTests.swift (six CLI cases including the four-file criterion and the no-suffix criterion).

Repro: `sleepy shot <url> --size 480 --size 1280 --theme light --theme dark --out header.png`.

Built on wt/shot2. `--sheet` lays a sweep's renders into one labeled mosaic at `--out`, beside the full-size files and their index.

Library: `ShotSheet` (Sources/SleepyHollow/Operations/ShotSheet.swift) — `Cell(capture:label:)`, a `Layout` that can be asserted without rasterizing, and `compose(_:maxSize:)` returning a `ShotCapture`. `ShotCapture(decoding: ShotImage)` is new, the inverse of `encoded()`, so the sheet composes the PNGs the page host already produced instead of rendering twice. Cell labels reuse `ShotGrid`'s Core Text machinery (`labelFont(ofSize:)`, `draw(_:at:font:in:)`, the gutter/ink/tick colours went from private to internal) — one text renderer for every label the readout pipeline draws.

Layout: columns = ceil(sqrt(N)), rows = ceil(N/columns); the sheet's longest side is capped at `--max-size` (default 2000). Gutters are reserved before the cells shrink, so labels stay legible at the sizes that need them.

The one thing worth a second opinion: **every cell is drawn at one shared scale factor**, sized from the *set's* bounding box, not fitted individually to its own cell. The first build fitted each capture to its cell and it was wrong on sight — a 390-wide render blew up to the same width as a 1280-wide one, which is exactly the comparison a breakpoint sheet exists to make. With a shared factor a narrow render reads as narrow and is letterboxed; each cell also gets a 1px outline so neighbouring white pages do not run together, and the label sits over the capture's own left edge rather than the cell's. Verified by eye against https://example.com/ at 390/800/1280 × light/dark.

Refusals: `--tile` (usage — the message names `--sheet` when that is what it collides with), and `--sheet` with nothing to sweep (a one-cell mosaic would also collide with its own full-size file, since only a varying axis gives that file a suffix).

Files: Sources/SleepyHollow/Operations/ShotSheet.swift; edits to ShotCapture.swift, ShotGrid+Draw.swift, ShotCommand.swift, ShotCommand+Sweep.swift.

Tests (red first): Tests/SleepyHollowTests/ShotSheetTests.swift (layout arithmetic, composition, the decode round-trip), Tests/SleepyGoldenTests/ShotSheetGoldenTests.swift (the criterion, plus both refusals).

Repro: `sleepy shot <url> --size 390 --size 1280 --sheet --out s.png` → s.png (mosaic), s-390.png, s-1280.png, index on stdout.

The suspected bug does not reproduce; no functional fix was needed.

`sleepyRectOf` (SleepyHelpers+Elements.swift) has always added `window.scrollX`/
`scrollY` to `getBoundingClientRect()`, from the same commit (`a38e03e`) that
introduced `sleepy.overflow`. That makes every rect `sleepyOverflow` reads
document-space and scroll-invariant: `box.left` shrinks by exactly what
`scrollX` grows, so `rect.x + rect.width` (box spill) and
`rect.x + max(rect.width, scrollWidth)` (content spill) never move when the
page scrolls. `viewportWidth` (`root.clientWidth`) is the viewport's own
size and never depends on scroll position either. So `boxRight > viewportWidth`
was already answering "does this exceed one viewport width from the
document's origin" — the scroll-independent question the ticket asked for —
without any correction.

Confirmed empirically, not just algebraically: scrolled `capture-wide.html`
(scrollTo 600,0) and to its own maximum scroll (1120,0 — exactly its own
overflowBy) and diffed the full `OverflowReport` against the unscrolled
baseline both times; byte-identical. Also tried `overflow-spill.html`, whose
`html`/`body` both set `overflow-x: hidden`, so `window.scrollTo` is a no-op
there (scrollX stays 0) — unhelpful as a scroll-variance fixture, consistent
with unscrolled/scrolled reports being identical there too (trivially).

I did NOT adopt the brief's suggested fix (`scrollX + viewportWidth` as the
new threshold) — verifying it would have been the wrong direction: at a
page's own maximum scroll, `scrollX + viewportWidth == documentWidth`
exactly, which would silently cancel the very violation this check exists to
catch. This matches the brief's own "a page scrolled by exactly its own
spill could hide a violation" warning, but the violation-hiding actually
happens if you add scroll-adjustment to viewportWidth (the naive
"corrected" fix), not in the current (unmodified) code.

Work done:
- Two new regression tests in Tests/SleepyHollowTests/OverflowOperationTests.swift:
  - "a horizontal scroll does not change the overflow report" — scrolls
    capture-wide.html by 600px, asserts the full report is unchanged.
  - "a page scrolled by exactly its own spill still reports the violation" —
    scrolls to exactly `violation.overflowBy` (the page's own max scroll),
    asserts the report is still unchanged (violation still present).
  - Both were GREEN on first run (confirmed via throwaway PROBE tests run
    first, deleted before the final commit-ready diff) — no fix landed
    because none was needed. Per the brief: "if a new test is green on first
    run, say so."
- Added a DocC/comment paragraph in
  Sources/SleepyHollow/Operations/SleepyHelpers+Overflow.swift explaining
  *why* the comparison is scroll-independent by construction (not by
  correction), citing the 2026-08-28 verification, and explicitly warning
  future readers off the `scrollX + viewportWidth` "fix" that would actually
  regress the max-scroll edge case. No production logic changed.

Reproduce with scripts/flake-hunt.sh under heavy spinner load, or by running the golden suite in two worktrees at once. Done on branch worktree-agent-a47f24a98bfde4432 (worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-a47f24a98bfde4432). 840 tests green, swiftformat --lint clean.

Shipped: LoadOptions.fileAccessRoot (URL?) and LoadOptions.Backdrop (.opaque default / .transparent), CLI --file-root <dir> and --transparent on the shared LoadFlagOptions (so every load verb and `sleepy open` carry them; both are load-shaping, so a --session invocation refuses them).

FINDING that overturns feedback finding 3: WKWebView.loadFileURL(_:allowingReadAccessTo:) does NOT grant fetch()/XHR against local files. Measured 2026-08-29 with a four-way probe against a new fixture file-fetch.html:
  load(URLRequest) + no pref        -> fetch "Load failed"
  loadFileURL + root + no pref      -> fetch "Load failed"
  load(URLRequest) + pref           -> reads the file (status 0)
  loadFileURL + root + pref         -> reads the file (status 0)
The grant that matters is the private WKPreferences key allowFileAccessFromFileURLs (a file: document has an opaque origin). fileAccessRoot therefore sets BOTH: loadFileURL (bounds subresource loading to the root, and refuses a page outside it) and the preference (unblocks script). WebKit does not bound the script grant to the root — a page under a fixtures root still read file:///etc/hosts. So that is a second private key, owned by one internal function WKPreferences.allowLocalFileReads(), same pattern and same ruling as the backdrop key. Feedback doc finding 3 corrected in place as a marked block quote.

Backdrop measurements: this WebKit answers _setDrawsBackground: and NOT setDrawsBackground:, so the responds(to:) guard probes the underscored selector. underPageBackgroundColor = .clear is neither sufficient (alpha stays 255) nor necessary (the KVC key alone gives alpha 0), so it is not set. Alpha survives ShotCapture.rasterize (hasAlpha, .copy), --scale 2, ShotTile cropping and PNG encoding with no change to the pipeline.

Canary proven red: neutering applyBackdrop's setValue and the preference call made 4 tests fail (alpha 255 in viewport / scale-2 / tiled shots, and the sibling fetch blocked); restored and green again.

Refactor (deviation): OpenCommand's hand-rolled flag->argv forwarding moved to a new LoadFlagOptions+SessionArguments.swift, because that seam is not compiler-enforced and a new flag silently does nothing inside a session. Two unit tests now round-trip flags -> argv -> parse -> LoadOptions for both new flags.

New files: Sources/SleepyHollow/Host/WKWebView+Backdrop.swift, Sources/SleepyHollow/Host/WKPreferences+LocalFiles.swift, Sources/SleepyCLIKit/Options/LoadFlagOptions+SessionArguments.swift, Tests/SleepyHollowTests/{BackdropTests,BackdropOptionTests,PageHostFileAccessTests,FileRootOptionTests}.swift, Tests/TestSupport/Fixtures/{backdrop.html,file-fetch.html,file-fetch-target.txt}.

data.text:
Fixed on branch worktree-agent-a8e0823be61588b23 (worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-a8e0823be61588b23). Full suite green: 842 tests, 128 suites, 71.7s, `swift test --quiet`, ambient load average ~90.

1. The client owns a deadline. `SessionClient.send` now bounds the whole exchange — connect, send, wait — at budget + `SessionClient.transportMargin` (2s). The deadline is a Task that cancels the `NWConnection`, not a task-group race: cancelling a Swift task does not interrupt an `NWConnection` receive, so a group would still wait on the child it cancelled. Failure is `.timeout` naming the session, the verb and the budget, with `sleepy sessions list` / `sleepy close <name>` as the next move.

   Budget threading: the first full-suite run went red on `archive --session` because the client's own default (30s) was *smaller* than the helper's (`open ... --budget 60000`). That was a second invented budget, exactly what the brief warned against. Fixed at the source: `SessionRecord` now carries `budget` (written by `SessionHost.start` from `page.budget`), and the client uses this invocation's `--budget` if given, else the helper's recorded one. `SessionClient.budget` is therefore `TimeInterval?` — nil means "the session's own". Wire change: an existing session directory written by an older build no longer decodes (BUILD stage, no compat spent) — `sessions prune` clears it.

2. The helper's `semaphore_wait_trap` is not ours. There is no `DispatchSemaphore`, no `DispatchQueue.sync`, no `runModal`-style block and no run-loop pump anywhere in `Sources/` (grep for Semaphore/.sync/waitUntilExit/CFRunLoop/NSApplication: only `NSApplication.shared.setActivationPolicy` and `NSPrintOperation.runModal`, neither of which blocks). Every step of the shot path is a continuation over an async WebKit API. So the wedged main thread is WebKit's own synchronous IPC to a starved WebContent process — the same starvation that, when it does return, surfaces as `takeSnapshot`'s bare `WKErrorDomain 1`. Nothing to fix on our side; the client deadline in (1) is the mechanism that keeps the tool honest about it.

3. The print crash was a dangling delegate. Both `.ips` files (1839, 1842) show `-[NSConcretePrintOperation _finishModalOperation]` -> `_CF_forwarding_prep_0` -> `___forwarding___` -> `-[NSObject __retain_OA]` -> throw, then `doesNotRecognizeSelector:`; the 1927 one is the same frames ending in a SIGSEGV inside `objc_msgSend`. That signature is a message to freed memory, not a wrong selector: `NSPrintOperation` does not retain its `didRun:` delegate, and the operation keeps running on its `NSThread` after the budget has already answered the caller — so `PrintRunner`, a local in `runModal`, was released while AppKit still held the pointer. Fixed by a main-actor `PrintRunner.pending` set: the runner joins before `runModal` and leaves when `didRun:` arrives. One that never calls back stays forever, on purpose (documented) — one small object per timed-out print.

Regression tests: `SessionClientDeadlineTests` over a new `StalledSessionHelper` double (an `NWListener` plus a `SessionRecord` naming this pid — smaller than a stalling `SessionHost`, no WebKit, no second process); upper bounds only. `PrintRunnerLifetimeTests` prints with budget 0 and asserts a weak reference to the runner survives the await — verified red (`observed -> nil`) by commenting out the single `pending.insert` line, then green.

Helper wedge confirmed to be WebKit sync IPC, not ours. Print crash was a dangling didRun: delegate — PrintRunner now retained in a pending set until the callback. Suite took 139 s this run with the HostGroup agent's suite running alongside.

HostGroup built, and the ruling's cache premise is falsified. (group-agent)

BUILT
- HostGroup (@MainActor final class): one WKWebsiteDataStore.nonPersistent(), an
  optional JarName and the JarStore, with the jar bookkeeping moved up one level
  — imported once per GROUP, exported after any member's load.
- PageHost.member(of:options:) — a throwing static factory rather than
  init(options:jars:group:), so ordinary construction stays non-throwing (only
  joining a group can be refused) and a member takes no `jars` argument at all
  (the group owns the store, so there is no second store to pick between).
  PageHost.group is public; ungrouped hosts are byte-identical to before, and
  PageHostJarTests passes unchanged.
- shot --sweep renders every combination through one HostGroup carrying --jar.
- scripts/measure-host-group.sh [LOADS] [SCRIPT_BYTES], driving an opt-in
  measurement suite (SLEEPY_MEASURE, SLEEPY_MEASURE_LOADS,
  SLEEPY_MEASURE_SCRIPT_BYTES, SLEEPY_MEASURE_ORDER).

THE FINDING — criterion 0BV cannot be met as written
A shared *non-persistent* WKWebsiteDataStore shares cookies but NO HTTP cache.
An ephemeral session has no network cache, and the cache that does serve a
repeated subresource lives in the web view's own content process, which two
views never share. Measured 2026-08-29, load average 17-30,
`scripts/measure-host-group.sh` — script fetches for two loads of one page:

  two views, one ephemeral store                         2
  two views, one ephemeral store + one WKProcessPool     2
  one view, two loads, ephemeral store                   1
  two views, one ephemeral store, first released         2
  two views, the persistent default store                1

WKProcessPool is API_DEPRECATED(... macos(10.10, 12.0)) with "no longer has any
effect" — exactly this package's floor — and the measurement agrees, so
HostGroup holds no process pool (deviation from the brief, which asked for one).

Per-load milliseconds, `scripts/measure-host-group.sh 6 3400000`, four runs:
  fresh first: fresh 285.0 / group 205.1 ms;  group first: fresh 204.0 / group 259.8
  fresh first: fresh 346.3 / group 201.9 ms;  group first: fresh 202.3 / group 296.9
Whichever arm runs SECOND lands at ~202 ms whichever it is. Grouping buys no
measurable per-load time; the apparent 30% win is warm-up. All six script
fetches happen in both arms.

So the plan's ruling is half wrong: the jar half holds and is built, the cache
half is unreachable from public API on a macOS 12 floor. Corrected in place in
the plan and in feedback finding 9; the whole measurement is
project/2026-08-29-host-group-cache.md; two routes to the real win (an isolated
persistent store, macOS 14 only; or re-using one web view across a sweep, which
the "one view, two loads" row shows is the whole saving) are in
project/backlog.md. Both need a ruling from Ben, not a leaf.

CRITERIA
  0BV  cannot be met as written — see above; a test now records the measured 2.
  AYZ  met: cookie set in one member's load is sent by the next, jar holds one
       copy, a member naming a different jar is a usage error.
  zOT  met: PageHostJarTests unchanged and green; PageHost.group == nil, own store.
  8Pt  half met: shot --sweep uses one group; the per-page cost is measured and
       is a wash.

Suite: swift test --quiet — 873 tests, 132 suites, passed in 128s.
swiftformat . --lint --config .swiftformat clean.

tasks.title: Session client hangs forever when the helper deadlocks under contention
tasks.description:

All three parked on SessionIntegrationGoldenTests' "matrix" session: each `sleepy _host --name matrix … --budget 60000` helper sat at 0% CPU with its main thread in `semaphore_wait_trap` (`sample <pid> 2`), and each client (`sleepy shot --session matrix`, `sleepy find --session matrix`) waited 7–11 minutes with no reply — far past the 60 s budget. Nothing timed out on either side; the suites would have hung indefinitely (killed by pid to unblock). Two related crash reports at 18:39 and 18:42 (`~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/sleepy-2026-08-29-18*.ips`): the helper aborting with doesNotRecognizeSelector inside `-[NSConcretePrintOperation _finishModalOperation]` on a secondary thread — the `pdf --session` path, cf. the 2026-08-28 gotcha about AppKit print callbacks.

Two things to fix, in order: (1) a session client must own a deadline — "nothing hangs" is the vision's rule, and today a helper that never replies hangs the client forever; (2) find the synchronous main-thread wait in the helper's shot path (WebKit sync IPC under contention, or ours) and the print-callback selector crash. Reproduce with scripts/flake-hunt.sh under heavy spinner load, or by running the golden suite in two worktrees at once. Reported by the host-api agent too: the same suite failed twice under concurrent agents, once with WKErrorDomain 1 from takeSnapshot, once with the print operation not finishing within 60 s.

Client-side deadline = budget + 2 s transport margin, cancelling the socket; SessionRecord now carries the helper's budget (wire change, pre-launch). Helper wedge confirmed to be WebKit sync IPC, not ours. Print crash was a dangling didRun: delegate — PrintRunner now retained in a pending set until the callback. Suite took 139 s this run with the HostGroup agent's suite running alongside.

data.title: Shots render CSS 3D transforms flat: no perspective, backface-visibility ignored
data.description: `sleepy shot` renders CSS 3D transforms flat: `perspective` has no effect, and `backface-visibility: hidden` is ignored. Pages that flip cards or tilt panels look wrong in shots, and a hidden back face paints over the front. Found 2026-10-27 while building a card-flip prototype. Compared against headless Chrome for Testing 153 (a `Page.captureScreenshot` over the DevTools protocol), which renders all cases as expected. ## Reproduce Serve this page and run `sleepy shot --size 1320x260 --wait-for 'js:[...document.images].every(i => i.complete)' -o out.png`: ```html ``` ## What happens - **A:** a plain rectangle, squeezed horizontally to the projected width. No perspective foreshortening: the near edge should be taller than the far one. - **B:** the orange BACK face shows, mirrored, on top of FRONT. `backface-visibility: hidden` has no effect, so whichever face is later in the DOM wins. ## Not a bug (checked) An `` inside a 3D-transformed box renders correctly once it has loaded. Images looked blank at first only because the shot fired before they finished loading; `--wait-for` fixes that. ## Likely cause (unverified) The offscreen snapshot may rasterize without 3D compositing, which flattens `preserve-3d` and skips back-face culling. Worth checking whether a different snapshot path (a compositing-backed snapshot) keeps 3D. ## Why it matters Card-flip interfaces can't be reviewed in sleepy. A page can hide the back face with `visibility` instead of relying on `backface-visibility`, but shots of a flip in progress still have to go through Chrome, because sleepy can't show the rotation.

data.title: Detect flattened 3D in a shot and say so
data.description:
Why: `shot` silently draws CSS 3D wrong. It drops perspective foreshortening, does no depth sorting under `preserve-3d`, and ignores `backface-visibility: hidden`, because `WKWebView.takeSnapshot` repaints in software with each layer's transform reduced to 2D affine. The pixels also disagree with `getBoundingClientRect()`, so crops and verdicts on a 3D element can be wrong. That is a plausible wrong answer, which the project rules out (2026-08-28-agent-feedback-synthesis.md § Rulings, "Never a plausible wrong answer": a stderr note over a misleading success). A compositor capture may fix the pixels later (sibling spike), but detection is needed in every outcome: it is the fallback wherever that capture can't run, and possibly what selects it.

What: when a shot's area (viewport, `--selector` element, `--rect`, or full page) contains an element whose flattened render would differ from the true 3D render, the library result records it, and the CLI prints a stderr note saying the shot draws CSS 3D flat, naming how many elements and a short selector for the first few, and pointing at Chrome or Ft2O4Q. Exit code stays 0 and the PNG is still written. The note is a correctness caveat, not a tip, so `--quiet` does not silence it. A sweep or `--tile` reports once per render, not once per file.

What counts: flag only what flattening actually changes. A 2D transform (rotate, scale, skew, translate) is not flagged. Neither is a bare 3D rotation with no perspective anywhere above it and no `preserve-3d`: an orthographic projection is exactly what the flattened paint draws, and Chrome agrees. Flag: a transform with perspective terms of its own (`perspective()`); a 3D transform under an ancestor whose `perspective` is not `none`; `transform-style: preserve-3d` with 3D-transformed descendants; `backface-visibility: hidden` on an element whose transform has a 3D component. Read it from computed style (`matrix3d` components, `perspective`, `transform-style`, `backface-visibility`), checking only elements that intersect the shot area.

Seams: the detector is a page-side helper beside the existing ones (Sources/SleepyHollow/Operations/SleepyHelpers*.swift, which run in Sleepy's isolated world). Its result rides on `ShotCapture`/`ShotImage` or the operation result — the builder's call; keep the wire type one shared `Friendly` struct. The CLI note belongs in Sources/sleepy/ShotCommand*.swift, following how `LoadCommand` reports page errors on stderr. Update the `shot` help text, the DocC, and project/recipes.md if it routes 3D questions.

Out of scope: fixing the pixels (the spike and the build leaf), `pdf` (not measured), `contrast`/`overflow` verdicts (a follow-up can reuse the detector; note it rather than build it).

Risks: false positives make agents ignore the note, so the no-flag cases need tests as much as the flag cases. Cost on huge pages: the walk must stay cheap (one pass, intersecting elements only).

data.title: Spike: compositor capture of a live hosted page
data.description:
Why: the only fix for flattened 3D is to capture what the compositor draws rather than what the software repaint draws. Window-server capture (ScreenCaptureKit) is ruled out because it needs Screen Recording permission. The candidate is public API: host the page in a live `OffscreenWindow` (`Rendering.live`, which uses the private `_setWindowOcclusionDetectionEnabled:`; SPI is approved for shot as of 2026-11-06), then render the web view's Core Animation layer tree with `CARenderer` into an off-screen Metal texture. Note that `CALayer.render(in:)` flattens 3D too, so it is not a candidate. The build leaf waits on this answer.

The question: can a live hosted `WKWebView`'s layer tree be rendered by `CARenderer` with true 3D (perspective foreshortening, preserve-3d depth sorting, backface culling), and at what cost? Answer each, with figures and the command that reproduces them:
1. Does it work? Does WebKit's UI-process layer tree carry real transforms and IOSurface-backed contents that `CARenderer` composites, or is it hosted remotely (a `CALayerHost` or context the renderer can't see into)? If it fails, say exactly where, and name any other route you found (e.g. an SPI snapshot that reads the compositor).
2. Fidelity: the 3D fixture (Ft2O4Q's reproduction plus project/2026-11-06-true-3d-shots.md's cases) compared against Chrome or the expected geometry; a flat page compared pixel-for-pixel with `takeSnapshot` at the same scale.
3. What it misses: video, WebGL/canvas, backdrop-filter, fonts that load late, and content outside the compositor's tiled coverage, which decides whether `--full-page` and `--rect` far below the fold can use it (scroll and stitch?).
4. Readiness: how to know the layer tree has committed the current frame before rendering, so the capture isn't a stale frame. This is the no-fixed-delays rule from project/2026-08-29-woodcase-harness-plan.md.
5. Cost: time per capture and memory, quiet and under the ambient load (check the load average and record it; no `yes` spinners on a loaded machine; see project/gotchas.md).
6. Live hosting side effects: does it also fix ND4YmR (rAF, CSS transitions, Web Animations; that issue has a fixture), and does `--wait-for idle` still settle on a page with an infinite rAF chain (project/2026-08-28-offscreen-window-host.md says it won't)?

Where the answer goes: a findings doc, project/2026-11-06-compositor-capture.md, following the house style of the other findings docs (every figure names its tool and flags). The probe goes in scripts/ so it can be re-run. Its code is otherwise disposable; it does not need to be shippable or TDD'd.

Out of scope: changing `shot`'s shipping behavior, or files the detection leaf owns (SleepyHelpers*, ShotCommand*).

data.title: JavaScript-off loading
data.description:
Why: Woodcase treats progressive enhancement as a first-class acceptance criterion, and "the page works with JS off" is exactly what a browser can settle. With no way to turn scripting off, they proved it over URLSession instead, a 133-line suite testing the server's markup rather than the browser's rendering (08-30 item 1).

What: a load option that disables the page's own JavaScript, in the library (`LoadOptions`, Sources/SleepyHollow/Core/LoadOptions.swift) and as a CLI load flag shared by every verb (Sources/SleepyCLIKit/Options/LoadFlagOptions*.swift), so `sleepy shot --no-js` and an embedder's three-line test both work.

Investigate first: `WKWebpagePreferences.allowsContentJavaScript` (public, macOS 11) disables page content scripts per navigation. The key question is what still works with it off. Sleepy's own helpers run in an isolated content world (InjectedScript, SleepyHelpers*), and `query`, `ax`, `eval --world isolated`, `contrast`, `overflow` and the wait engine all depend on injected script. Measure which verbs keep working, and decide what `eval --world page` does (refuse with a teaching error, presumably). `--wait-for idle` and `js:` predicates also need an answer. `<noscript>` content must render.

Open questions: the flag's name and shape (`--no-js`, `--scripting off`) is the builder's call, following existing flag style; anything that changes a verb's contract is Ben's.

data.title: A trusted press
data.description:
Why: there is no keyboard act verb. Woodcase hand-copies an untrusted `KeyboardEvent` dispatch into four test files, and nothing built that way can exercise an `isTrusted` check or a real default action: typing into a field, Tab focus movement, Enter submitting a form, Escape closing a dialog (08-30 item 2).

What: `PageHost.press(_:)` in the library and a `sleepy press` act verb beside click/fill/submit, delivering keys the way a user's keyboard would, so `isTrusted` is true and default actions run.

Investigate first: whether WebKit delivers trusted key events to a windowless or off-screen-hosted WKWebView. Likely route: synthesize `NSEvent` key events and send them through `WKWebView.keyDown(with:)`/`keyUp(with:)`; that may need the view to be first responder in an `OffscreenWindow`, and possibly a key window (see project/2026-11-06-true-3d-shots.md and spike leaf B3dXgQ question 7, which measures a key-window override; coordinate rather than duplicate). Modifiers, named keys (Enter, Tab, Escape, arrows) and text input (IME aside) all need a shape.

Seams: act verbs live in Sources/SleepyHollow/Operations/ (ClickOperation, ActionScript*) and Sources/sleepy/ClickCommand.swift etc.; the session and one-shot paths both apply.

Open questions for Ben: the key syntax (`Enter`, `Meta+K`, a string to type) and whether `press` targets a selector (focus it first) or whatever has focus. If trusted delivery proves impossible, bring that back rather than shipping untrusted events under a trusted-sounding name: that would be a plausible wrong answer.

data.description:
Why: every Woodcase bench hand-writes the same two helpers: five copies of a 6-line `ask()` that decodes `evaluate`'s JSON-text return, and five of a polling `waitFor(_:_:within:)` (08-30 item 3). data.text: First finding (exploratory probe, scratch): WebKit on macOS 27.0.1 uses UI-side compositing — the UI-process layer tree under WKWebView.layer is real WKCompositingLayers with real 3D transforms (sublayerTransform m34 = -1/600 for perspective:600px) and CAIOSurface contents (tiles + composited layers). No CALayerHost. CARenderer(mtlTexture:) on that tree renders true 3D: trapezoid foreshortening and backface culling (FRONT shows, BACK culled), where takeSnapshot on the same live view draws flat (squeezed rect, mirrored BACK). Gotchas: CARenderer.layer = x removes x from its superlayer (must re-insert after), needs CATransaction.flush() before render (first try without it rendered blank white), output is vertically flipped (CA bottom-left origin). Probe being built at scripts/compositor-probe.sh.

Probes (2026-11-06, debug `sleepy shot`/`query`, load avg ~30, scratch fixtures probe.html/probe2.html):
- Bare rotateY(60deg) with no perspective: pixels at x 75–175, same as getBoundingClientRect (75–175). The flat paint is orthographic, so the brief's no-flag claim holds in WebKit. Chrome is not installed here, so the "Chrome agrees" half is unverified.
- rotateY under perspective:200px on the parent: rect 37–160, pixels 75–175. Flattening changes it.
- Perspective on the grandparent, through a flat parent (positioned or static): the rect is orthographic (325–425). A flat parent cuts perspective off, so the walk goes up only through used preserve-3d parents.
- backface-visibility:hidden with rotateY(180deg), no perspective: the flat paint draws it (the true render hides it).
- transform: perspective(200px) alone (only m34 set): pixels equal the rect. Not flagged.
- preserve-3d keeps computed 'preserve-3d' under overflow:hidden, opacity:.99, filter, isolation:isolate and clip-path, but the geometry is flat for all five. The detector checks the used value.
Detector: window.sleepy.flattened3D (SleepyHelpers+Transforms.swift). Reasons: perspectiveFunction (m14/m24/m44), perspectiveAncestor, preserve3D, hiddenBackface (only when facing away). Results are pruned to the outermost flagged element.
Follow-up (not built): contrast/overflow could reuse flattened3D to caveat their verdicts on 3D elements.

data.title: Wait backstop polls at 1 Hz on a hidden page: nested setTimeout is throttled
data.description: `PredicateWatch`'s page-side backstop is a self-rescheduling `setTimeout(check, 16)` loop. On a hidden (windowless or Rendering.hidden) page WebKit throttles a nested timer chain to 1 Hz from about its tenth tick, so after ~170 ms the backstop polls once a second, and `--wait-for` predicate latency falls back to the 250 ms host backstop, approaching 1 s when the main thread is busy. Measured 2026-11-06, project/2026-11-06-compositor-capture.md question 8 (`scripts/compositor-probe.sh timers 10`). `MessageChannel` is not throttled (62 Hz), and a live host runs timer loops at 50 Hz. Fix options: drive the backstop with a MessageChannel or another unthrottled source, or let it ride on live hosting if decision BJkByM makes that the default. Needs a regression test that measures backstop cadence past the tenth tick.

Measured 2026-11-06 (Tests/TestSupport/Fixtures/no-js.html, a throwaway probe test via PageHost, `swift test --filter`, load avg 30-90):

1. `WKWebpagePreferences.allowsContentJavaScript = false` ALONE is a half switch.
